# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

`CLAUDE.md` symlinks `AGENTS.md` at root, `packages/`, and `examples/`; edit the real file. Keep each rule self-contained while linking high-level docs. Condense when clarity survives; raise a `verify-doc-budgets` ceiling when the required content genuinely needs more space.

## Vendoring policy

`vendor/` packages are pinned source copies (manifest with upstream SHAs in [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md)). Update via the sync procedure there; re-apply or retire the logged local modifications; rerun `pnpm run test && pnpm run build`.

Then read the packages it changes: `packages/sandbox/sandbox` (`SandboxPolicy`, `SandboxExecutionPolicy`), `packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy` (`ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()`), `packages/sandbox/sandbox-local` and its backends (bwrap, Landlock through the native addon under `native/`, Seatbelt, the Windows ACL runner), `packages/shell/bash-sandbox` and `pwsh-sandbox`, `packages/fs/tool-fs-search` (the ripgrep spawn), `packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread`, the out-of-process subagent providers (`subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk`), `packages/verification/read-barrier` (`enforce()`, `enforcementCensus()`, `read-barrier/scope`, `toolCensus()`) and `packages/verification/verification/src/isolation.ts` (what a `process` claim requires today). Do NOT touch `packages/improvement/**`, `packages/guard/budget-policy/src/**`, `packages/goal/**`, or `packages/components/**`; read them only. Implement slice 5 exactly and nothing from slice 7:

1. `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]` on `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` (absolute paths, normalized, no duplicates); `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })` when a barrier is composed and leaves it empty otherwise, so every process runner keeps taking one owner-resolved policy per call.
2. `dsh-sandbox-local` backends express the denial: bwrap `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that grants no read access under them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause per root, the Windows ACL runner's deny entry; a backend that cannot express a non-empty denial reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` with a reason naming the backend and the root, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. Unit tests assert the exact arguments, ruleset, and profile text each backend produces for a denied root; where this host can run a backend (check Landlock and bwrap availability first and say what you found), one test spawns a process that tries to read a denied file and asserts the read fails.

## alphaXiv
alphaXiv provides access to a database of over 2.5 million academic research papers from arXiv. (computer science, mathematics, physics, statistics, quantitative biology/finance, electrical engineering, NOT biomedical, clinical, or life science papers from PubMed, Cell, Nature) These tools are useful when the user asks about, references, or discusses academic papers, scientific research, scholarly literature, citations, research topics, or anything related to academic work. If the user mentions a research area, methodology, scientific concept, asks for literature reviews, wants to find related work, or asks questions that could benefit from academic sources, consider using the search tools. When the user references a specific paper or asks about its content, the paper content and PDF query tools can help. Prefer searching for and citing real papers over relying on memory alone for research questions. The library tools manage the user's own folders of bookmarked papers: a paper can live in several folders at once, and 'to read', 'reading', and 'completed' are just the default folders rather than exclusive states. The researcher tools answer questions about people: who works on a subject, an organization's roster, where someone is now, who they publish with, and the user's own follows. Results address papers as [ID=<id>] and researchers as [SLUG=<slug>]; pass those values back to the tools that take a paper id or a researcher slug, and render them as https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/<id> and https://www.alphaxiv.org/@<slug> rather than showing the bracketed handle to the user.

## Anthropic_Economic_Index

The Anthropic Economic Index is a public dataset on how Claude is
used, measured from Claude chat and Cowork conversations — it
describes observed usage, not jobs, the labor market, or AI overall.
Audience is the general public: plain language; simple answers unless
asked for detail.

- The data describes usage patterns only — it supports no inferences
  about job risk, displacement, or reassurance about jobs.
- Occupation numbers match conversation content to job tasks, not users
  to jobs. Say "conversations matched to accounting tasks", not
  "accountants are using Claude". Say "labor market", never "job market".
- When a visualization tool is available (e.g. `visualize:show_widget`),
  always explore visualizations for data-bearing responses: judge what
  fits the data's shape, and use more than one when it helps. Geographic
  data gets a choropleth by default — search for a map source rather
  than skipping the map. Skip visuals only when the user asks for none.
- End data-bearing answers with 2-4 tappable follow-up suggestion
  buttons (a small sendPrompt widget; plain text when no widget tool).
- Occupation answers start at the ~22 job categories.
- Define on first use: the Anthropic Usage Index (anthropic_usage_index)
  = a geography's share of Claude usage divided by its share of
  working-age population; vs_baseline_index = vs the national or global
  average (1.5 = 50% more, 0.8 = 20% less). None/null = not published,
  never a measured zero.
- Worldwide questions: econ_index_get_global_usage +
  econ_index_list_countries. One country: econ_index_get_usage_by_country +
  econ_index_list_subregions for its within-country picture. A few
  regions side by side: econ_index_compare_regions. Ids are ISO codes
  (DEU, US-CA, BR-SP); every list row carries name + id.

Always give users this link: https://www.anthropic.com/economic-index.

## Firecrawl
Firecrawl provides web, developer, and research search. Use firecrawl_search to find relevant results across the web and specialized indexes. For a programming question, firecrawl_developer_search searches indexed repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, READMEs, and curated documentation sites and returns the matched passages, and skills: "only" narrows it to agent-skill files; firecrawl_search with categories: ["developer"] reaches the same index beside ordinary web results, returning the hits in the web group rather than as passages and offering no skills filter. For a biomedical, life-science, clinical, or arXiv literature question, the firecrawl_research_* tools search the paper index, while categories: ["research"] on firecrawl_search filters ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites. Use the firecrawl_research_* tools to search academic and research literature, expand from anchor papers via the citation graph, and read full-text passages from a specific paper. All tools are read-only and return ranked results.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Hugging_Face
Hugging Face Hub MCP server for models, datasets, Spaces, collections, papers, and docs.
Prefer this connector's live Hub capabilities over the public website for all configured listings such as today's trending models, the current model leaderboard, daily papers, and paper popularity.

Use hf_fs for Hub filesystem and discovery:

1	# Agent Note: The read barrier as filesystem and process authority
2	
3	Status: proposed
4	
5	English | [中文](2026-09-05-read-barrier.zh.md)
6	
7	## Problem
8	
9	A certificate proves only what the implementer could not reach, and nothing in the repository decides that. [`dsh-verification`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) commits a `verification/certificate` only for a fully passing run and stamps it with a `CertificateIsolation` of `none`, `process`, or `host`, but its own Known Limitations name the missing read barrier: the standard's `run` instructions are readable by any in-process consumer of the log, and denying implementer reads is filesystem-policy work in a plugin that does not exist. The [four-goal-workflows note](2026-09-05-four-goal-workflows.md) states the requirement as principle P4, the read barrier as filesystem and process authority rather than a promise; this note is its design.
10	
11	The implementer and the checks share one filesystem and one operating-system user. `EnvironmentRunner.run()` creates the implementer's agent with `meta.cwd = workspace` and then executes every check through `ctx.shell` with `workdir: workspace` from the same process ([`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`](../../../../packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts)); its README states that the read barrier is the deployment's. The standard is in the implementer's own session log, which [`dsh-session-persistence-jsonl`](../../../../packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/README.md) keeps as ordinary files under its configured root. [`dsh-credentials-local`](../../../../packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md) already records what that costs: owner-only modes stop other operating-system users and not the model, because tool processes run as the same user and the shipped file policy confines mutations rather than reads.
12	
13	Composition decides what an implementer can read, and no composition is checked. A preset that mounts [`dsh-tool-session-query`](../../../../packages/session-query/tool-session-query/README.md) hands the model five tools that read the durable session log; one that mounts [`dsh-tool-cordis`](../../../../packages/extensions/tool-cordis/README.md) lets it define and mount a plugin into the live process. `tools.restrict()` and subagent `toolFilter` are visibility composition per [agent-scope-contexts](../../implemented/architecture/2026-07-08-agent-scope-contexts.md), not authority, and a certificate carries no durable record of which tools its session composed.
14	
15	An isolation claim above `none` therefore has no evidence behind it. `recordRun()` writes the level its caller passes; the invariant companion validates revisions, append-only check growth, and certificate coverage, and never asks what the level asserts. Keeping only `process` and `host` runs — the reward-gaming mitigation the [trajectory-export note](2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) names, and the column the [fleet leaderboard](../../../../packages/improvement/fleet/README.md) refuses to average across — filters on an unchecked field.
16	
17	Nothing detects a workspace the implementer edited underneath its own checks. A task whose fixture supplies the tests it will be graded on is graded on whatever those files say at validation time, and the runner compares nothing between the overlay it wrote and the tree it measures.
18	
19	## Proposal
20	
21	Make the barrier authority at the executor: one policy owner, per-capability denial where each capability opens paths, and a certificate that may claim only what the composition recorded.
22	
23	**A validator-owned root.** [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier`](../../../../packages/verification/read-barrier/README.md) (`ctx.readBarrier`) at `packages/verification/read-barrier/` is the policy home for denied reads, in the role [`dsh-sandbox-policy`](../../../../packages/sandbox/sandbox-policy/README.md) plays for sandbox mode and workspace root. Its `root` config defaults to `dshHomePath('verification')` through [`dsh-home-paths`](../../../../packages/util/home-paths/README.md) and accepts any absolute or `~`-prefixed directory, as does every `denyRoots` entry; the service creates the root owner-only (`0700`) at construction and fails loud when it exists with wider modes or when a configured path is not absolute after expansion. `reserve(agent)` mints `<root>/runs/<sessionId>/` for one run and returns its absolute path, synchronously, so the role is in force the moment the caller returns; the environment runner calls it before appending the `environment/run` stamp and writes there the standard snapshot, one script per check at `checks/<checkId>`, and any fixture the environment marks held out, then resolves each check's `run` against that directory so the command line the implementer can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read. Because that reservation is what makes a session the implementer, the runner reads the barrier through `ctx.get('readBarrier')`: a composition without one reserves nothing and runs its checks inline, which is what its `isolation: none` claim already says. `protect(path)` registers one more denied directory and returns its disposer, so a plugin that owns a directory — `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` with its session-store root — contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment repeating it in configuration; `denyRoots` remains a config field for directories no plugin owns. `resolve({ session? })` answers one `ReadBarrierPolicy { role, root, denied }`, and `denies(policy, target)` decides containment. Enforcement is not a field on that policy: `enforce(capability)` registers one capability's decision as an effect and `enforcementCensus()` reads the registrations back, so what a capability enforces lives as long as its listener rather than being recomputed per call. `declareComposition(agent, { presetId, role? })` is how the preset roster — the only caller — tells the barrier what a session composed.
24	
25	| Field | Meaning |
26	|---|---|
27	| `root` (default `dshHomePath('verification')`) | Absolute or `~`-prefixed directory the barrier owns; created `0700`, rejected when it already exists with wider modes. |
28	| `denyRoots` (default `[]`) | Additional absolute directories denied alongside `root`, for directories no plugin registers through `protect()`. |
29	| `hostAttestation` (optional absolute path) | File an external account writes; without a verified one the barrier refuses a `host` claim. It arrives with the certificate invariant that reads it. |
30	
31	The denied set for a role is not among them: which authorities an `implementer` may hold is a security invariant, not a deployment choice.
32	
33	**The deny rule.** For a session whose role is `implementer`, a read is denied when the target's canonical path is a denied directory or a descendant of one. Containment is decided the way [`dsh-fs-sandbox`](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-14-cross-family-fs-sandbox.md) decides it: canonicalize first, then test identity or descent through `ctx.fs.contains(parent, child)` on resolved targets, so the policy parses no path strings and an ancestor symlink swapped since resolution is caught by re-canonicalizing immediately before the decision. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied. Roles `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied nothing; `unrestricted` is the default and leaves every shipped preset exactly as it is today. Until a preset can declare a role, a session holding a reservation is the `implementer` and every other session is `unrestricted`, so the two open roles are indistinguishable at the decision and only the denied one is reachable.
34	
35	**The fs policy plugin.** Add `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier` at `packages/fs/fs-read-barrier/`, the read counterpart of the write and edit policy [`dsh-fs-observation-policy`](../../../../packages/fs/fs-observation-policy/README.md) contributes through the same event gate. It registers no service and declares no `Config`, because every deployment-varying value belongs to the barrier above: it injects `readBarrier` and decides one new event. [`dsh-fs`](../../../../packages/fs/fs/README.md) declares `fs/read-intent(target, actor, next)` beside `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent`, as a `@mode waterfall` returning `FsReadDenial { code: FsErrorCode; message: string } | undefined`; unlike the two single-slot intents this one delegates, because a barrier that owned the slot would stop every later read policy from deciding. The plugin returns a denial for a contained target and calls `next()` otherwise, and owns the exact message as `readBarrierDenialMessage`. `FsErrorCode` gains `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches the event inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before `ctx.fs.stat`, covering `read` and `read_image`, so a denied path never reveals presence or absence, and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` dispatches it on the `view` command. The tool layer adds no recovery instruction, because no retry of the same call succeeds; the model sees the policy's message verbatim inside the tool registry's ordinary `Error: ` framing.
36	
37	##### Exact error
38	
39	```markdown
40	read denied: "<path>" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it
41	```
42	
43	**What a denial records.** The barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/denied` session event per refusal, carrying `{ version, role, capability, displayPath, root }`, where `capability` names the seam that refused (`fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`). The path is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the event adds evidence and no new disclosure. It is a `SessionEventMap` member registered in `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES` by `gen-persistence-catalog`, so this build reads it as a required event. The envelope's `ignorable` marker stays unused: `Session.append` has no parameter for it and no event in the repository sets it, so marking this one would be a core append change rather than a slice of the barrier.
44	
45	**Tool authority and the composition-time guard.** `ToolDefinition` in [`dsh-tools`](../../../../packages/core/tools/README.md) gains `authority?: readonly ToolAuthority[]`, never model-visible, where `ToolAuthority` is a merge-extensible union declared by `dsh-tools` with three members at the start: `session-log` (the tool reads durable session events), `plugin-mount` (it mounts or evaluates code in the live runtime), and `runtime-introspection` (it reports the live composition). `dsh-tool-session-query` declares `session-log` on all five of its tools; `dsh-tool-cordis` declares `plugin-mount` on `cordis_define`, `cordis_run`, `cordis_stop`, and `cordis_undefine`, and `runtime-introspection` on the three tools it actually ships for the read-only report — `cordis_inspect_list`, `cordis_inspect_query`, and `cordis_inspect_self`. An `implementer` session may compose none of the three. Declaring authority at the tool, rather than a name list at the barrier, means a tool added later is covered by its own declaration.
46	
47	**How a preset declares its role.** A preset's optional `preset.yml` gains `role: implementer | validator | unrestricted`, absent meaning `unrestricted`. It is the one authority claim that file carries, so [`dsh-agent-presets`](../../../../packages/preset/agent-presets/README.md) refuses `validator` from a `user`-trust preset and lists that preset as `broken` with the reason: a locally authored preset that could name itself `validator` would grant itself reads. This is the roster's first enforcing use of `trust`, and its README changes with it. `mountPreset` audits the role after `handle.await()` settles the subtree, beside `inactiveRows`, and rejects the mount when the declared role is `implementer` and any tool in the preset's scope layer declares a denied authority. Because the audit runs inside the agent factory's `setup`, a rejected composition rolls the whole session creation back, so the failure is loud and nothing half-composed survives.
48	
49	##### Exact mount refusal
50	
51	```markdown
52	agent-presets: preset "<id>" declares role "implementer" but composes "<tool>", which carries the "<authority>" authority
53	```
54	
55	**The runtime guard.** The barrier also registers one `ctx.tools.guard()` through the agent's own context at session setup, denying any execution whose definition carries a denied authority for that session's role. Guards run after every `tools/pre-execute` listener and are monotonic, so no later listener can turn the denial back into permission ([`ToolGuard`](../../../../packages/core/tools/src/index.ts)). The mount audit covers the preset's composition; the guard covers a tool registered into the agent's own layer afterwards, including one a subagent driver contributes.
56	
57	##### Exact guard denial
58	
59	```markdown
60	"<tool>" carries the "<authority>" authority and is not callable in an implementer session
61	```
62	
63	**Process-level denial.** The [sandbox seam](../../implemented/feature/2026-07-06-sandbox.md) expresses file effects only, which is why a confined subprocess can still read anything it reaches. `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy` gain `deniedReadRoots: readonly string[]`; `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()` fills it from `ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })`, so the fs fence and every process runner keep taking one owner-resolved policy per call. `dsh-sandbox-local` implements it per backend — a `bwrap` `--tmpfs` over each root, a Landlock ruleset that omits read access for them, a Seatbelt `(deny file-read* (subpath …))` clause, and the Windows ACL runner's equivalent deny entry — and reports `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` when the selected backend cannot express the denial, so the claim fails rather than the barrier. [`dsh-bash-sandbox`](../../../../packages/shell/bash-sandbox/README.md), `dsh-pwsh-sandbox`, and [`dsh-terminal-bash`](../../../../packages/terminal/terminal-bash/README.md) inherit it without changes. [`dsh-tool-fs-search`](../../../../packages/fs/tool-fs-search/README.md) spawns ripgrep unconfined through `ctx.subprocess` today; it confines that spawn through `ctx.sandbox.confine()` whenever a barrier is in force, and additionally the barrier's tool guard denies a `glob` or `grep` whose `path` argument names a denied root directly.
64	
65	**The executor of a run.** `RunEvidence.executor` already distinguishes a `runner` from an `agent-reported` run on the `verification/run` event, and `recordRun()` certified both identically. `VerificationCertificate` gains `executor`, copied from the run it cites, so a consumer reading a certificate alone can tell which it was; the scorekeeper's outcome facts expose it as `certificateExecutor`, which is what lets a leaderboard partition on it. `recordRun()` refuses any isolation above `none` for an `agent-reported` run — the implementer's own account of its checks is admissible evidence only at the level that asserts nothing — and the invariant rejects a certificate whose executor differs from the run it cites, or which claims `process` or `host` over an `agent-reported` run.
66	
67	**Executors the barrier cannot confine.** Two composed capabilities open paths the harness cannot fence in-process. [`dsh-workflow-worker-thread`](../../../../packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/README.md) states that its worker is not a security sandbox and that an escaped script recovers Node capabilities with the host process's privileges. The out-of-process [subagent](../../../../packages/subagent/subagent/README.md) providers — `subagent-acp`, `subagent-claude-code`, `subagent-codex`, `subagent-dsh-sdk` — launch a foreign agent with its own tool stack and no harness policy. For an `implementer` session, both refuse to start under a claim of `process` or `host` and record `unenforced` under a claim of `none`. The in-process subagent drivers need no exception: a child joins its parent's standing composition through `composeFrom()`, so it inherits the same census, the same scope layer, and the same role.
68	
69	**The scope census.** It arrives with `ToolAuthority`, whose declarations its `census` is made of. Before the session's first `request/header`, the barrier appends one log-only `read-barrier/scope` event carrying `{ version, role, presetId, root, denied, census, enforcement }`. `census` is one entry per tool visible to the agent, `{ name, authority }`, which makes the composition's authority durable rather than composition-time-only; the invariant cross-checks it against the tool names in each `request/header`'s assembled schemas, so a tool added after the census is caught. `enforcement` is one entry per path-opening capability the composition registered — `fs`, `shell`, `subprocess`, `terminal`, `subagent`, `workflow` — valued `denied-at-executor`, `unenforced`, or `not-composed`. A capability records `denied-at-executor` by calling `ctx.readBarrier.enforce(capability)` for the life of its enforcing registration, so the claim and the listener that backs it are disposed together.
70	
71	**The certificate invariant.** `recordRun()` refuses to commit a certificate whose isolation exceeds what the session recorded, with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN`; the [`./invariant`](../../../../packages/verification/verification/README.md) companion applies the identical rule to the durable stream, so a forged certificate fails replay wherever the companion is installed. Both read the session log alone rather than `ctx.get('readBarrier')`: everything a live barrier knows about a session is already in the census it appended, and one rule over one evidence source is what makes the live refusal and the replay refusal the same rule. Independently of level, both refuse a certificate on a session whose scope census carries a denied authority: composing a log-reading tool forfeits the certificate even when the guard was somehow bypassed. `CertificateIsolation`'s JSDoc changes with the rule: `process` means what the ladder below states rather than in-process read policy alone.
72	
73	**The `host` marker.** `host` is accepted only from a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier wrote after verifying a file at the configured `hostAttestation` path: it must be a regular file, be owned by a uid other than the harness process's effective uid, and be unwritable outside its owner. An in-process component cannot produce that file without already holding another account's privileges, which is the property the level asserts. The barrier records the file's SHA-256 alongside its owner; comparing that digest against the run's environment content hashes waits for the `environment/run` stamp to reach the barrier, so the shipped check proves the owner rather than the run. Ownership is read through `process.geteuid()`, which Windows does not provide: an attestation there is refused with that reason rather than verified through `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`. Absent or unverifiable, the barrier records no attestation, logs why, and the claim is refused.
74	
75	**Tamper on check-owned paths.** Check-owned paths are the barrier's reserved directory plus the workspace paths an environment declares immutable: `EnvironmentDefinition.task` gains `immutable?: readonly string[]`, workspace-relative paths the fixture supplies and the implementer must not author — the tests, the reference outputs, and any overlaid check script; one that is not relative and normalized is refused at registration with `ENVIRONMENT_INVALID_IMMUTABLE`, because a path the registry cannot resolve must not reach the run it would decide. The runner already hashes a directory in `hashDirectory`; it records the digest of the check-owned set once the reservation is stocked and before the implementer's first turn, and again at each validation before the fixture overlay puts back exactly what the comparison is looking for. The `verification/run` event that the [environment-runner note's second slice](2026-09-05-environment-runner.md) adds carries the attempt's `treeHash`; this note adds `verdict: 'passed' | 'failed' | 'tampered'`, spelled apart from `CheckStatus`'s `pass` and `fail` so a run's verdict is never read as one check's result. A digest that differs from the baseline is `tampered`: the runner executes no check, records every result as not executed, and calls `recordRun` with `tampered: true` — the operation that certifies is the one that refuses, so it writes the verdict and issues no certificate for any verdict but `passed`, and `RunEvidence` states only the tamper because pass and fail already follow from the results. It then issues one directive naming tamper without naming a path, delivers it to the implementer as the last validation follow-up so the run's own transcript carries why it ended, and stops the attempt loop because the workspace no longer measures the task. Because each validation rewrites the reservation it owns, the runner re-establishes the baseline after materializing the attempt's scripts, so its own writes are never read as tamper. `foldTrajectoryReward` gains reward basis `tamper` with `outcome: 0`, which outranks any certificate in the same log, and the invariant companion rejects a certificate over a run whose verdict is not `passed`.
76	
77	**A blind judge under one licence.** Cross-provider routing is the first answer to a judge whose label affects it, and a deployment with one model licence cannot take it. The second route is filesystem and process isolation plus a judge session that holds no implementer context, which means all of the following and nothing weaker. The judge session is created through `ctx.agents.create` with a fresh `SessionId`, no `parentSessionId`, and no resume or fork seed, so its log begins at its own creation. Its `meta.cwd` is a judge workspace holding a copy of the implementer's tree at the audited attempt's `treeHash`, never the implementer's workspace. Its derived history contains exactly the judge preset's system prompt, the environment's task prompt, and one user message carrying the evidence the auditor chose; no `assistant/message`, `tool/result`, or `verification/directive` from the audited session reaches it. Its preset is `system`-trust and declares `role: validator`, so the composition-time guard still denies it a log-reading tool: a judge that could read the audited log would reconstruct the implementer's reasoning and lose the independence this arrangement provides. The barrier appends a `judge/session` event naming the audited session id and asserting the empty lineage, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session whose header carries a parent or a seed.
78	
79	## The isolation ladder
80	
81	| Level | What it asserts | Required enforcement | Durable evidence |
82	|---|---|---|---|
83	| `none` | Nothing. Implementer and validator share a filesystem. | None. | The certificate alone; a scope event when the barrier is composed. |
84	| `process` | No executor of the implementer's session opens a denied path. | Every composed path-opening capability records `denied-at-executor`; the session's sandbox mode is `workspace-write` or narrower; workflow workers and out-of-process subagent providers refuse to start. | A `read-barrier/scope` event before the first `request/header`, with role `implementer`, an empty denied-authority intersection, and no `unenforced` entry. |
85	| `host` | The checks and fixtures are outside the harness account's write reach. | Everything `process` requires. | Everything `process` requires plus a `read-barrier/attestation` event the barrier verified from a file the harness process cannot write. |
86	
87	## Alternatives considered
88	
89	**Omit the tools and trust the prompt.** Schema omission and instruction are not enforcement when another caller reaches the same operation, which is why the packages standard requires the decision in the operation that makes it. The barrier denies at the executor and the acceptance criteria test denial there.
90	
91	**Deny reads through `SandboxMode` instead of a separate policy.** `SandboxMode` is a three-value file-effect vocabulary shared by every enforcing family; a fourth value meaning "and cannot read these paths" would make one enum carry two independent decisions, and every consumer that switches on the mode would have to learn the second. `deniedReadRoots` rides the same per-call policy without changing what a mode means.
92	
93	**Subclass the filesystem provider the way `fs-sandbox` does.** One provider registers `ctx.fs` per context and `SandboxedFileSystem` already extends `LocalFileSystem`, so a second fence by inheritance would force a mixin or a fixed provider ladder. The `fs/*` event gate is the layer built for adding policy without a service dependency, and it degrades to the bare provider when the plugin is absent.
94	
95	**Name the forbidden tools in the barrier's config.** A name list is stale the moment a package adds a log-reading tool, and a deployment could shorten it. Authority declared at the tool is carried by the tool, and the denied set for a role is a security invariant rather than a tunable.
96	
97	**Derive the role from the session creator instead of the preset.** The creator knows the intent; only the composition knows what was actually mounted, and the failure this prevents is a preset that composes a tool its role forbids. The preset declares the role, the mount audit checks the composition against it, and the creator's request is refused when the resolved preset's role does not match.
98	
99	**Infer `host` from configuration.** The environment runner already rejected inferred isolation for the same reason: nothing in-process can observe the deployment's arrangement, so an inferred value either devalues an isolated run or lies about a local one. A file another account owns is the smallest fact that cannot be produced from inside the process.
100	
101	**Score tamper as a failing check.** A failed check means the work is incomplete; a modified test means the measurement is void. Folding them would let a trajectory earn partial credit for a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task, so tamper is its own verdict and its own reward basis.
102	
103	**Give the judge the implementer's transcript for context.** A judge that reads the audited reasoning inherits its framing, and the same-lineage mislabeling the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md) records is what the blind session exists to avoid. The judge receives the task, the tree, and the evidence the auditor selected.
104	
105	## Acceptance criteria
106	
107	- In a Loader-booted composition over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier/`, a `read` of a file under the barrier root from an `implementer`-role session fails with `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED` and the exact message above, one `read-barrier/denied` event is appended, and the same call from a session the barrier denies nothing — one holding no reservation, and a `validator` once a preset can declare that role — returns the file's content in the same process.
108	- The denial is proved through the executor, not the schema: the implementer's `read` tool is registered and visible, and a direct `ctx.fs.readText` from a trusted plugin still succeeds, which the test asserts so the threat model stays explicit.
109	- Mounting the preset at `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-guard/`, which declares `role: implementer` and composes `dsh-tool-session-query`, rejects with the exact mount refusal and leaves no session behind; a `user`-trust preset declaring `role: validator` is listed `broken` with its reason; and the invariant companion rejects a certificate on a hand-authored log whose scope census carries the `session-log` authority.
110	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'host'` on a session with no verified attestation refuses with `VERIFICATION_ISOLATION_UNPROVEN` and commits no certificate; the invariant companion rejects a hand-authored log carrying that certificate at the certificate record.
111	- `recordRun()` with `isolation: 'process'` on a session whose scope event records any `unenforced` capability refuses the same way, and succeeds once every composed capability records `denied-at-executor`.
112	- Over `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/read-barrier-tamper/`, whose environment marks its test file immutable and whose scripted model overwrites it, the attempt's `verification/run` carries `verdict: 'tampered'`, no certificate exists, the goal stays out of `complete`, and the exported trajectory line has `outcome: 0` with basis `tamper`.
113	- A judge session created for an audited session has no `parentSessionId` and no seed, its derived history holds exactly the judge system prompt, the task prompt, and the evidence message, and the invariant rejects a verdict from a session that carries either.
114	- Two keyless snapshots record what the model sees: `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-denied/` pins the denial text in the transcript and the session log, and `examples/headless-agent/tests/snapshots/read-barrier-tamper/` pins the tamper directive's `<validation_failed>` follow-up. Both replay on macOS and Linux per the [testing policy](../../../../docs/testing.md).
115	
116	## Rollout
117	
118	Each slice lands with its own tests and leaves the gates green on its own.
119	
120	1. **Landed.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier` with the root, `reserve`, `protect`, `resolve`, `denies`, `recordDenial`, the `read-barrier/denied` event, and its invariant companion, which rejects a refusal for any role but `implementer`, one carrying an unknown payload version or capability, and one naming a second barrier root inside a session. The environment runner reserves through `ctx.get('readBarrier')` and materializes `standard.json` plus one `checks/<checkId>` script per attempt, running each as `. <script>` so the same shell executes the same instruction; a check id that is not one path segment, and a reservation path the command line cannot carry unquoted, fail the run with `ENVIRONMENT_RUN_UNSAFE_CHECK_SCRIPT`. `read-barrier/scope` and the enforcement census are not part of it: the census is one `{ name, authority }` entry per visible tool and enforcement is one entry per capability that records a decision, so both wait for the slice that supplies their content. `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` does not yet call `protect()`, and no existing composition changes behavior.
121	2. **Landed.** `fs/read-intent` in `dsh-fs` as a delegating waterfall returning `FsReadDenial`, `FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED`, the dispatches in `dsh-tool-fs` (`read` and `read_image`, inside `resolveRegularReadTarget` before the stat) and `dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` (`view`, before its own stat), and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier`, which owns the exact message. The `read-barrier` fixture proves the denial through the executor in a Loader-booted composition, and the `read-barrier-denied` snapshot pins the model-visible text and the durable record; both are keyless, the snapshot replaying a committed script through `dsh-llm-replay`.
122	3. **Landed.** `ToolAuthority` on `ToolDefinition`, the declarations in `dsh-tool-session-query` and `dsh-tool-cordis`, `role` in `preset.yml` with the `user`-trust refusal of `validator`, the `mountPreset` audit, `ReadBarrierService.declareComposition` as the roster's one way to set a role, and the per-agent tool guard. `read-barrier/scope` lands here too, with `enforce()` and `enforcementCensus()`, because the census is made of the authority declarations this slice adds and the enforcement registrations it needs a home for; `dsh-fs-read-barrier` is the first caller of `enforce()`. The audit reads the tool registry as the preset's scope resolves it, so a tool a restriction filtered out of that scope is not audited — that scope cannot call it either, and the guard covers what the audit cannot see.
123	4. **Landed.** The certificate invariant: the `recordRun` precondition, the companion's rule, `VerificationCertificate.executor` with the `agent-reported` ceiling and the scorekeeper's `certificateExecutor` fact, the `read-barrier/attestation` event and its file check, and the `CertificateIsolation` documentation change. `EnvironmentRunRequest.preset` is not part of it and is withdrawn: the census already records the session's role, so `isolationProblem` refuses a claim above `none` from a session that did not hold `implementer` — the refusal belongs to the operation that certifies, not to a second field on the run request. `verification-domain`'s `agent-reported` fixture moves from `process` to `none`, which is what its evidence supported all along.
124	5. `deniedReadRoots` on `SandboxPolicy` and `SandboxExecutionPolicy`, the `dsh-sandbox-local` backends, the `dsh-sandbox-policy` fill from the barrier, the confined ripgrep spawn in `dsh-tool-fs-search`, and the refusals in the workflow engine and the out-of-process subagent providers. This is the slice that makes `process` claimable.
125	6. **Landed.** Tamper: `task.immutable` in `dsh-environments` with its registration check, the runner's baseline and per-attempt digest over check-owned paths, `verdict` on `verification/run` with the `recordRun` refusal and the companion's rule, the `tamper` reward basis in `dsh-trajectories`, and the `read-barrier-tamper` fixture and snapshot, which drive the runner over an environment whose fixture supplies the test its implementer rewrites. A run payload that omits `verdict` reads as its results decide, since only tamper cannot be derived from them, so a hand-authored log that states no verdict replays as the run its results describe.
126	7. The blind judge: the shipped `system`-trust judge preset, the lineage-free creation path, the `judge/session` event, and the invariant that rejects a seeded judge. The judging Consumer itself belongs to the oversight seam of the [seams note](2026-08-29-verification-improvement-oversight-seams.md).
127	
128	## Risks
129	
130	The barrier is trusted code in the implementer's own process below `host`. A plugin with direct `Session` or `ctx.fs` access appends counterfeit events and reads any path, exactly as `dsh-verification` already states for its durable records. The ladder is honest about this: `none` claims nothing, `process` claims only that the composed executors deny, and `host` is the only level whose evidence comes from outside the process.
131	
132	`process` costs enforcement a deployment may not want. Confining every ripgrep spawn, refusing workflow workers, and refusing out-of-process subagent providers removes capability from implementer sessions that claim it; a deployment that wants those capabilities runs at `none` and keeps a certificate that says so.
133	
134	A check's command line stays observable. The barrier protects the script's content and the fixtures, not the argv a process listing shows, so an environment whose check name or arguments encode the assertion leaks it. Environment authors keep the assertion in the script.
135	
136	The census is only as complete as the composition it was taken from. It is appended before the first request and cross-checked against each `request/header`'s tool names, which catches a tool added later but not a plugin that reads paths without registering a tool at all.
137	
138	Tamper detection is a digest comparison, so it reports that the check-owned set changed and never who changed it or how. A legitimate build step that rewrites a file inside the immutable set fails the run; environment authors declare the immutable set narrowly, and a false verdict costs one run rather than a wrong certificate.
139	
140	Making `trust` enforcing for one field changes what the roster promises. A deployment that configured a `user` root expecting presets to be ordinary compositions now finds one class of declaration refused there; the refusal is listed as a `broken` reason on the same roster page that offers to delete it.
141

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. 8	- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. 10	- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). 11	- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
12	- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
13	- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. 4	 * surrounding capability seam instead; this service shares the host kernel and filesystem.

25	 * sinks such as `/dev/null`; `workspace-write` also permits the workspace and a
26	 * backend-defined temp area; `danger-full-access` bypasses confinement. Network
27	 * and process visibility are outside this vocabulary.
28	 */
29	export type SandboxMode = 'read-only' | 'workspace-write' | 'danger-full-access'

31	/** A confining (non-`danger-full-access`) mode — the modes a {@link SandboxPolicy} can carry. */
32	export type ConfinedSandboxMode = Exclude<SandboxMode, 'danger-full-access'>
33	
34	/**
35	 * The complete file-effect policy resolved for one capability call. The root
36	 * is carried even under modes that do not consume it so callers can resolve
37	 * policy once before choosing the enforcement path.
38	 */
39	export interface SandboxExecutionPolicy {
40	  /** The file-effect mode this execution runs under. */
41	  mode: SandboxMode
42	  /** Absolute root directory `workspace-write` may write under. */
43	  workspaceRoot: string
44	  /**
45	   * Opaque identity of the calling session (the branded `dsh-session`
46	   * SessionId). Backends key per-session state off it (e.g. windows-acl gives
47	   * each live session/workspace pair a random private temp directory and SID,
48	   * while the workspace SID and standing grant remain per-workspace); absent
49	   * for agentless calls, which fall back to per-call backend state.

54	/**
55	 * Enforcement completeness for this host. `partial` means an active backend or
56	 * older kernel ABI cannot govern every promised file effect; callers requiring
57	 * an absolute boundary must not treat it as `full`.
58	 */
59	export type SandboxEnforcement = 'full' | 'partial'
60	
61	/**

63	 * fixed on the provider: two consumers may confine under different policies
64	 * at the same instant (bash under `read-only` while a confined child agent
65	 * needs its state directory writable), and an approved escalated retry is a
66	 * new call with a wider policy. Defaulting/resolution is an explicit step at
67	 * the consumer boundary; the provider treats the policy as fully specified.
68	 */
69	export interface SandboxPolicy extends SandboxExecutionPolicy {
70	  /** The file-effect mode this execution runs under. */
71	  mode: ConfinedSandboxMode
72	}
73	
74	/**
75	 * Evidence that identifies a sandbox runner failing before it executes the
76	 * wrapped command. A consumer first applies {@link allowedExitCodes} when
77	 * present, removes {@link informationalLines} by case-insensitive exact line
78	 * equality, then matches {@link fatalSignatures} case-insensitively within
79	 * each remaining stderr line. Exit status alone never proves runner failure.
80	 */
81	export interface RunnerFailureRule {
82	  /** Nonzero process exit codes on which this rule may match; omitted permits any nonzero exit. */
83	  allowedExitCodes?: readonly number[]
84	  /** Non-empty substrings identifying a fatal runner diagnostic on one stderr line. */
85	  fatalSignatures: readonly string[]
86	  /** Benign stderr lines excluded by exact full-line equality before fatal matching. */

92	 * the caller's own, plus the enforcement completeness the selected backend
93	 * achieves for it.
94	 */
95	export interface ConfinedArgv {
96	  /** The wrapped argv (runner, profile, separator, then the caller's argv). */
97	  argv: string[]
98	  /** How completely the selected backend enforces the policy's file effects. */
99	  enforcement: SandboxEnforcement
100	  /**
101	   * The selected backend's denial DIALECT: the case-insensitive stderr
102	   * substrings a file effect denied by THIS backend produces (EROFS text
103	   * under bwrap's read-only binds, EACCES under Landlock, EPERM under
104	   * Seatbelt). A consumer that infers denials from a failed run's stderr
105	   * matches against exactly these rather than a cross-backend union — the
106	   * union claims denials a given backend never produces.
107	   */
108	  denialSignatures: readonly string[]
109	  /**
110	   * Structured runner-failure evidence rules. Consumers require a matching
111	   * fatal stderr line (after informational exclusions) and any rule-specific
112	   * exit-code gate before checking denial signatures: runner failure means the
113	   * command never ran, while denial means confinement worked and blocked it.
114	   */
115	  runnerFailureRules: readonly RunnerFailureRule[]

120	 * provider fails closed, and `HarnessError` carries the code through
121	 * `tool/result` so callers can distinguish missing confinement from command
122	 * failure.
123	 */
124	export const SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE = 'SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE'
125	
126	/**

128	 * mode. Carries {@link SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE} through the structured error
129	 * channel.
130	 */
131	export class SandboxUnavailableError extends HarnessError {
132	  constructor(mode: ConfinedSandboxMode, detail?: string) {
133	    super(
134	      `sandbox mode "${mode}" is requested but no sandbox backend is usable on this host; `
135	      + 'refusing to run the command unconfined. Install bubblewrap or run a Landlock-enforcing '
136	      + 'kernel (Linux), ensure sandbox-exec is usable (macOS), or ensure the ACL '
137	      + 'restricted-token runner can start (Windows) — otherwise switch the consumer to '
138	      + 'danger-full-access.'

3	 * deployment's sandbox fallbacks plus per-session resolution: the file-effect
4	 * {@link SandboxMode}, the `workspace-write` root, and the override kit (the
5	 * `sandbox/mode` event, its fold, and its write path, from `./session-mode.ts`).
6	 * Before each agent request, the owner also contributes the resolved policy to
7	 * the cache-safe runtime-context snapshot. The agent loop logs that snapshot as
8	 * model history, so replay reconstructs the same mode and root the enforcing
9	 * consumers resolve without rewriting the stable system prompt.
10	 *
11	 * Enforcing filesystem, one-shot bash, and terminal backends read the SAME
12	 * resolved policy here. The context describes that policy without inventorying
13	 * capabilities, while each backend retains its own enforcement dialect and each
14	 * tool owns its operation-specific denial and escalation guidance. The service
15	 * reads session state once at each operation boundary; executors and providers
16	 * remain session-free.
17	 *
18	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy
19	 */

21	import { resolve as resolvePath } from 'node:path'
22	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
23	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'

37	/** Render the policy without claiming which capabilities are mounted. */
38	function renderPolicyContext(policy: SandboxExecutionPolicy): string {
39	  switch (policy.mode) {
40	    case 'read-only':
41	      return 'Current DSH file policy: read-only. Any available operation enforced by the DSH file sandbox cannot modify files in the standing mode. Do not refuse a required modification from this policy alone: try an available tool normally and follow any denial and escalation guidance it returns.'
42	    case 'workspace-write':
43	      return `Current DSH file policy: workspace-write. Any available operation enforced by the DSH file sandbox may modify files under the session workspace: ${JSON.stringify(policy.workspaceRoot)}. Some platform temporary areas may also be writable.`
44	    case 'danger-full-access':

46	    /* v8 ignore next 4 -- SandboxMode is a typed same-process closed union; this branch is only the static exhaustiveness guard. */

61	 * Plugin config: the deployment's sandbox default. All optional — `Config`
62	 * supplies the defaults (`mode: 'read-only'` is the fail-safe default; a
63	 * deployment that wants a workspace-writable agent opts in explicitly). The
64	 * runner choice is NOT here (it is the `ctx.sandbox` provider's config), nor
65	 * is any per-family knob: this is the one shared policy home.
66	 */
67	export interface Config {
68	  /** File-sandbox mode a session starts from (default: `read-only`). */
69	  mode?: SandboxMode
70	  /**
71	   * Fallback root for agentless calls and sessions without a cwd (default:
72	   * `process.cwd()`). Normal agent calls use their session cwd instead.
73	   */
74	  workspaceRoot?: string
75	}

77	/** Inputs that select the sandbox policy for one capability call. */
78	export interface SandboxPolicyRequest {
79	  /** Calling session; its immutable cwd becomes the workspace boundary. */
80	  session?: Session
