85	/**
86	 * The sandbox-policy service (`ctx.sandboxPolicy`). Owns the deployment
87	 * default mode, fallback workspace root, and current request-time policy
88	 * section. Tool layers call {@link resolve} for each execution so a session's
89	 * mode log and immutable cwd travel together to every enforcing capability.
90	 */
91	export class SandboxPolicyService extends Service {
92	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
93	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
94	    mode: z.union(['read-only', 'workspace-write', 'danger-full-access'] as const).default('read-only'),
95	    // No schema default: process.cwd() is resolved in the constructor so the
96	    // stored root is always absolute regardless of how it was supplied.
97	    workspaceRoot: z.string(),
98	  })
99	
100	  /** The deployment default mode — the fallback beneath a session override. */
101	  readonly defaultMode: SandboxMode
102	  /** The absolute `workspace-write` fallback root for calls without a session cwd. */
103	  readonly workspaceRoot: string
104	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
105	    super(ctx, 'sandboxPolicy')
106	    // schemastery (static Config) already filled `mode`; the cast records that
107	    // runtime fact. `workspaceRoot` has NO schema default, so its fallback to
108	    // the process cwd is real branching, resolved absolute either way.
109	    this.defaultMode = config.mode as SandboxMode
110	    this.workspaceRoot = resolveWorkspaceRoot(config.workspaceRoot ?? process.cwd())
111	
112	    ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], (scope: Context) => {
113	      scope.systemPrompt.context({
114	        name: 'sandbox:policy',
115	        order: 110,
116	        text: (context) => {
117	          const session = context.agent?.session
118	          return session === undefined
119	            ? ''
120	            : renderPolicyContext(this.resolve({ session }))
121	        },
122	      })
123	    })
124	  }
125	
126	  /**
127	   * Resolve the complete policy for one capability call. An approved explicit
128	   * mode outranks the session's last `sandbox/mode` event, which outranks the
129	   * deployment default. A session cwd is its workspace-write boundary; the
130	   * configured root is the fallback for agentless calls and sessions without a
131	   * cwd.
132	   * @param request - optional session and approved mode override.
133	   * @returns the fully resolved per-call mode and absolute workspace root.
134	   */
135	  resolve(request: SandboxPolicyRequest = {}): SandboxExecutionPolicy {
136	    const { session } = request
137	    return {
138	      mode: request.mode ?? (session === undefined ? undefined : this.overrideOf(session)) ?? this.defaultMode,
139	      workspaceRoot: resolveWorkspaceRoot(session?.header.cwd ?? this.workspaceRoot),
140	      ...session === undefined ? {} : { sessionId: session.id },
141	    }
142	  }
143	
144	  /**
145	   * Read the session override without applying the deployment default.
146	   * @param session - session whose log supplies the override.
147	   * @returns the last logged mode, or `undefined` without one.
148	   */
149	  overrideOf(session: Session): SandboxMode | undefined {
150	    return effectiveSandboxMode(session.events)
151	  }
152	}

86	  const probe = spawnSync(seatbeltExec, [...seatbeltProfileArgs({ mode: 'read-only', workspaceRoot: '/' }), '--', 'true'], {
87	    timeout: timeoutMs,
88	    stdio: 'ignore',
89	  })
90	  return probe.status === 0

93	/**
94	 * Functional windows-acl probe: run the runner in read-only mode (zero grants,
95	 * no ACL mutation) around `cmd /c exit 0` — exit 0 means the runner created
96	 * the restricted token and spawned the child under it. The win32 chain is a
97	 * sole candidate, so the product never probes; the probe exists for override
98	 * chains and mirrors the other rungs' shape.
99	 */
100	function defaultProbeWindowsAcl(runnerInvocation: string[], timeoutMs: number): boolean {
101	  const program = runnerInvocation[0]
102	  if (program === undefined) return false
103	  const probe = spawnSync(program, [
104	    ...runnerInvocation.slice(1),
105	    '--workspace', tmpdir(), '--temp', tmpdir(), '--mode', 'read-only',
106	    '--', 'cmd', '/c', 'exit', '0',
107	  ], {
108	    timeout: timeoutMs,
109	    stdio: 'ignore',
110	  })
111	  return probe.status === 0
112	}

140	/** The chain's verdict: which runner confines, and how completely it enforces. */
141	type SelectedRunner = { runner: 'bwrap' | 'landlock' | 'seatbelt' | 'windows-acl'; enforcement: SandboxEnforcement }

144	interface AclTempCapability {

150	/**
151	 * The runner chain per platform — selection is BY PLATFORM first, probes
152	 * second: a platform's chain is probed in preference order only when it has
153	 * MORE than one candidate (probing arbitrates; it does not re-validate a
154	 * choice that has no alternative). A platform with no chain fails closed at
155	 * `confine()`. Linux prefers `bwrap` (its mount profile is closest to the
156	 * mode vocabulary) over the Landlock launcher; darwin has exactly one
157	 * candidate, selected without any probe.
158	 */
159	const PLATFORM_CHAINS: Record<string, readonly SelectedRunner['runner'][]> = {
160	  linux: ['bwrap', 'landlock'],
161	  darwin: ['seatbelt'],
162	  // The Windows restricted-token runner (@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl):
163	  // a sole candidate, selected without a probe — its execution-time refusal
164	  // fails closed through its stderr signature (windows-acl-run:) and exit 127.
165	  win32: ['windows-acl'],
166	}

168	/**
169	 * Enforcement completeness a rung claims when selected WITHOUT a probe (a
170	 * chain of one). `bwrap` and Seatbelt govern every promised file effect by
171	 * construction, so the claim is a profile fact; `landlock` is listed for the
172	 * table's totality but is unreachable unprobed today (the Linux chain has
173	 * two rungs, so it is only ever selected through its probe, whose report is
174	 * what distinguishes full from per-ABI-partial — and the launcher additionally
175	 * self-reports partial enforcement on stderr at every confined run).
176	 */
177	const STATIC_ENFORCEMENT: Record<SelectedRunner['runner'], SandboxEnforcement> = {
178	  bwrap: 'full',
179	  landlock: 'full',
180	  seatbelt: 'full',
181	  // WRITE_RESTRICTED needs Everyone in both restricting lists for process
182	  // initialization. An external object that grants Everyone write access
183	  // therefore remains writable, and NTFS hard links can alias a granted
184	  // workspace file to a path outside it. The backend enforces the remaining
185	  // ACL-addressable surface but must not advertise the absolute promise.
186	  'windows-acl': 'partial',
187	}

189	/**
190	 * A probe bound must be a positive finite number: Node treats
191	 * `spawnSync({ timeout: 0 })` as NO timeout, so an unvalidated 0 would
192	 * silently mean "unbounded" — the opposite of what the field promises.
193	 */
194	function assertPositiveFinite(name: string, value: number): void {
195	  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) {
196	    throw new Error(`sandbox-local: ${name} must be a positive finite number`)
197	  }
198	}

200	/**
201	 * The denial dialect each runner's kernel speaks — the case-insensitive stderr substrings a
202	 * denied file effect produces under it, carried on every wrap (the seam's
203	 * `ConfinedArgv.denialSignatures`).
204	 */
205	const DENIAL_SIGNATURES = {
206	  bwrap: ['read-only file system'],
207	  landlock: ['permission denied'],
208	  seatbelt: ['operation not permitted'],
209	  // pwsh/.NET: "Access to the path '...' is denied."; cmd: "Access is denied.";
210	  // node EACCES: "permission denied".
211	  'windows-acl': ['access is denied', 'access to the path', 'permission denied'],
212	  runnerCommand: ['read-only file system', 'permission denied'],
213	} as const satisfies Record<SelectedRunner['runner'] | 'runnerCommand', readonly string[]>
214	
215	/** The windows-acl runner's documented failure exit (its own RUNNER_FAILURE_EXIT contract, distinct from Landlock's 125). */
216	const WINDOWS_ACL_RUNNER_FAILURE_EXIT = 127

218	/**
219	 * Runner-owned fatal diagnostics. Landlock has a versioned exit-125 plus
220	 * fatal-line launcher-failure contract. Bubblewrap's current fatal paths exit
221	 * 1 but its public contract does not reserve that status, while sandbox-exec
222	 * publishes no launcher-failure status; those backends remain signature-only.
223	 * The windows-acl runner prints `windows-acl-run: <detail>` on every
224	 * runner-side failure and exits 127 — the rule is exit-gated on that status
225	 * so a confined command that merely PRINTS the signature (or a runner
226	 * cleanup failure reported on a non-zero child exit) is never misclassified
227	 * as "the command did not run". Keep the Landlock tuple aligned with the
228	 * assembled snapshot fixture at
229	 * `examples/acp-agent/tests/fixtures/partial-landlock-sandbox.ts`.
230	 */
231	const RUNNER_FAILURE_RULES = {
232	  bwrap: [{ fatalSignatures: ['bwrap: '] }],
233	  landlock: [{
234	    allowedExitCodes: [LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT],
235	    fatalSignatures: [`${LAUNCHER_BIN}: `],
236	    informationalLines: [`${LAUNCHER_BIN}: partial enforcement (older Landlock ABI)`],
237	  }],
238	  seatbelt: [{ fatalSignatures: ['sandbox-exec: '] }],
239	  'windows-acl': [{ allowedExitCodes: [WINDOWS_ACL_RUNNER_FAILURE_EXIT], fatalSignatures: ['windows-acl-run: '] }],
240	} as const satisfies Record<SelectedRunner['runner'], readonly RunnerFailureRule[]>

243	 * Local process-sandbox provider. Registers as `ctx.sandbox`. Caches the
244	 * chain verdict and, on the windows-acl rung, the write grants
245	 * ({@link AclWriteGrant}: the standing workspace-root grant per workspace
246	 * and the revocable private-temp grant per live session/workspace pair, the
247	 * latter revoked on provider dispose); the one-time probes spawn nothing
248	 * else.

250	export class LocalSandboxProvider extends SandboxProvider {
251	  // Inline schema call: the config catalog walks `static Config` statically.
252	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
253	    runnerCommand: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
254	    runnerFailureSignatures: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
255	    probeTimeoutMs: z.natural().default(5_000),
256	  })

258	  /** Test hook (mirrors the bash executors' `internals`). */
259	  internals: SandboxInternals = {}
260	
261	  private readonly runnerCommand: string[] | undefined
262	  private readonly configuredRunnerFailureSignatures: string[]
263	  private readonly probeTimeoutMs: number
264	  /** Cached chain verdict; undefined until the first confined wrap needs it. */
265	  private selectedRunner: SelectedRunner | 'unavailable' | undefined
266	  /**
267	   * Server-lifetime write grants (windows-acl rung): the STANDING
268	   * workspace-root grant per workspace (its ACE is the cross-session reuse
269	   * cache and outlives the provider — never revoked) and the REVOCABLE
270	   * private-temp grant per live session/workspace pair (revoked on provider
271	   * dispose).
272	   */
273	  private readonly workspaceGrants = new Map<string, AclWriteGrant>()
274	  private readonly tempCapabilities = new Map<string, AclTempCapability>()
275	
276	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
277	    super(ctx)
278	    // The schema (static Config) defaults every field — the casts record
279	    // those runtime facts. An empty runnerCommand means "not configured":
280	    // use the platform chain.
281	    const runner = config.runnerCommand as string[]
282	    const runnerFailureSignatures = config.runnerFailureSignatures as string[]
283	    if (runner.length === 0 && runnerFailureSignatures.length > 0) {
284	      throw new Error('sandbox-local: runnerFailureSignatures requires runnerCommand')
285	    }
286	    if (runner.length > 0 && runnerFailureSignatures.length === 0) {
287	      throw new Error('sandbox-local: runnerCommand requires at least one runnerFailureSignatures entry')
288	    }
289	    if (runnerFailureSignatures.some(signature => signature.trim().length === 0 || /[\r\n]/u.test(signature))) {
290	      throw new Error('sandbox-local: runnerFailureSignatures entries must be non-empty single-line strings')
291	    }
292	    this.runnerCommand = runner.length > 0 ? runner : undefined
293	    this.configuredRunnerFailureSignatures = runnerFailureSignatures
294	    this.probeTimeoutMs = config.probeTimeoutMs as number
295	    assertPositiveFinite('probeTimeoutMs', this.probeTimeoutMs)
296	    // The temp grants are revoked with the provider: a clean server
297	    // shutdown leaves no temp ACEs behind (workspace ACEs stand by design —
298	    // the reuse cache; an unclean shutdown leaves them for the next
299	    // provision's exact-ACE skip).
300	    ctx.effect(() => () => {
301	      this.revokeAclGrants()
302	    })
303	  }

305	  /**
306	   * Wrap `argv` in the selected runner's invocation for `policy` — the configured
307	   * `runnerCommand` when present (the operator's assertion, no probe), else the platform
308	   * chain's runner speaking its own profile dialect.
309	   *
310	   * @param argv - the exact argv the caller is about to spawn.
311	   * @param policy - the file-effect policy this execution runs under.
312	   * @returns the wrapped argv plus the selected backend's enforcement completeness, denial
313	   *   signatures, and structured runner-failure rules; throws the fail-closed
314	   *   `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` error when the platform has no usable runner.
315	   */
316	  confine(argv: readonly string[], policy: SandboxPolicy): ConfinedArgv {
317	    if (this.runnerCommand !== undefined) {
318	      return {
319	        argv: [...this.runnerCommand, ...bwrapProfileArgs(policy), '--', ...argv],
320	        enforcement: 'full',
321	        denialSignatures: DENIAL_SIGNATURES.runnerCommand,
322	        runnerFailureRules: [{ fatalSignatures: this.configuredRunnerFailureSignatures }],
323	      }

325	    const selected = this.selectRunner(policy.mode)
326	    const runnerArgv = this.runnerArgv(selected.runner, policy)

328	      argv: [...runnerArgv, '--', ...argv],
329	      enforcement: selected.enforcement,

331	      runnerFailureRules: RUNNER_FAILURE_RULES[selected.runner],

335	  /** The selected rung's runner invocation (program + profile arguments) for one policy. */
336	  private runnerArgv(runner: SelectedRunner['runner'], policy: SandboxPolicy): string[] {
337	    switch (runner) {
338	      case 'bwrap': return ['bwrap', ...bwrapProfileArgs(policy)]
339	      case 'landlock': return [this.landlockLauncher(), ...landlockProfileArgs(policy)]
340	      case 'seatbelt': return [this.seatbeltExec(), ...seatbeltProfileArgs(policy)]
341	      case 'windows-acl': return this.windowsAclRunnerArgv(policy)

343	    }
344	  }

346	  /**
347	   * The windows-acl runner argv for one policy. With a calling session (the
348	   * policy's `sessionId`) under workspace-write, the grants are materialized
349	   * once per provider lifetime — the standing workspace-root grant per
350	   * workspace and a revocable, RANDOM private-temp capability per live
351	   * session/workspace pair. The runner receives `--write-sid` plus
352	   * `--temp-write-sid` and grants nothing itself. Agentless workspace-write
353	   * calls pass the ambient temp ROOT and no SID flags: the runner creates and
354	   * removes a random private child directory for that one invocation.
355	   * @param policy - the resolved per-call policy.
356	   * @returns the runner invocation.
357	   */
358	  private windowsAclRunnerArgv(policy: SandboxPolicy): string[] {
359	    const sessionId = policy.sessionId
360	    if (sessionId === undefined || policy.mode === 'read-only') {
361	      return [
362	        ...this.windowsAclRunnerInvocation(),
363	        '--workspace', policy.workspaceRoot,
364	        '--temp', tmpdir(),
365	        '--mode', policy.mode,
366	      ]
367	    }
368	    const temp = this.materializeAclGrant(sessionId, policy.workspaceRoot)

370	      ...this.windowsAclRunnerInvocation(),
371	      '--workspace', policy.workspaceRoot,
372	      '--temp', temp.dir,
373	      '--mode', policy.mode,
374	      '--write-sid', workspaceWriteSid(policy.workspaceRoot),
375	      '--temp-write-sid', temp.writeSid,
376	    ]
377	  }

379	  /**
380	   * Materialize one workspace-write policy's ACEs once per provider
381	   * lifetime. The workspace SID and standing root grant are shared by the
382	   * workspace. The temp directory is random and carries a distinct SID, so
383	   * another session on the same workspace cannot use the shared workspace
384	   * SID to enter it. A fresh provider always chooses a new path; crash
385	   * residue therefore cannot collide with or authorize a resumed session.
386	   * Fail-closed: a half-materialized temp grant is revoked and its directory
387	   * removed before the error propagates.
388	   * @param sessionId - the policy's calling-session identity.
389	   * @param workspaceRoot - the resolved policy root.
390	   * @returns the pair's private temp directory and write capability.
391	   */
392	  private materializeAclGrant(sessionId: SessionId, workspaceRoot: string): AclTempCapability {
393	    assertTempRootOutsideWorkspace(workspaceRoot, tmpdir())
394	    const writeSid = workspaceWriteSid(workspaceRoot)
395	    if (!this.workspaceGrants.has(workspaceRoot)) {
396	      const grant = AclWriteGrant.create(writeSid)
397	      try {
398	        grant.add(workspaceRoot, true)
399	      } catch (error) {
400	        // Free the SID; a standing ACE (if the apply succeeded before a
401	        // post-apply throw) is the intended end state, not an error
402	        // artifact — nothing to revoke.
403	        try {
404	          grant.dispose()
405	        } catch (cleanupError) {
406	          throw new AggregateError([error, cleanupError], 'sandbox-local windows-acl workspace grant failed and its cleanup also failed')
407	        }
408	        throw error
409	      }
410	      this.workspaceGrants.set(workspaceRoot, grant)
411	    }
412	    const key = JSON.stringify([String(sessionId), workspaceRoot])
413	    const existing = this.tempCapabilities.get(key)
414	    if (existing !== undefined) return existing
415	    const tempDir = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-'))
416	    const tempSid = tempWriteSid(tempDir)
417	    let grant: AclWriteGrant | undefined
418	    try {
419	      grant = AclWriteGrant.create(tempSid)
420	      grant.add(tempDir)
421	    } catch (error) {
422	      const cleanupFailures: unknown[] = []
423	      if (grant !== undefined) {
424	        try {
425	          grant.dispose()
426	        } catch (cleanupError) {
427	          cleanupFailures.push(cleanupError)
428	        }
429	      }
430	      try {
431	        this.removeTempDir(tempDir)
432	      } catch (cleanupError) {
433	        cleanupFailures.push(cleanupError)
434	      }
435	      if (cleanupFailures.length > 0) {
436	        throw new AggregateError([error, ...cleanupFailures], 'sandbox-local windows-acl temp grant materialization failed and its cleanup also failed')
437	      }
438	      throw error
439	    }
440	    const capability = { dir: tempDir, writeSid: tempSid, grant }
441	    this.tempCapabilities.set(key, capability)
442	    return capability
443	  }

445	  /**
446	   * Dispose every write grant (provider dispose): the revocable temp ACEs
447	   * are revoked, the private temp directories this provider created are
448	   * removed, and every SID allocation is freed; the standing workspace ACEs
449	   * stay (the reuse cache). Cleanup failures are reported, not thrown:
450	   * cordis teardown must not be aborted by grant cleanup. A crash skips all
451	   * of it, but a new provider never reuses the residue's random path or SID;
452	   * OS temp hygiene (or manual removal) eventually reclaims it.
453	   */
454	  private revokeAclGrants(): void {
455	    if (this.workspaceGrants.size === 0 && this.tempCapabilities.size === 0) return
456	    const failures: unknown[] = []
457	    for (const grant of [...this.workspaceGrants.values(), ...[...this.tempCapabilities.values()].map(capability => capability.grant)]) {
458	      try {
459	        grant.dispose()
460	      } catch (error) {
461	        failures.push(error)
462	      }
463	    }
464	    for (const { dir } of this.tempCapabilities.values()) {
465	      try {
466	        this.removeTempDir(dir)
467	      } catch (error) {
468	        failures.push(error)
469	      }
470	    }
471	    this.workspaceGrants.clear()
472	    this.tempCapabilities.clear()
473	    if (failures.length > 0) {
474	      this.ctx.logger.warn(`sandbox-local: windows-acl grant cleanup completed with ${failures.length} failure(s)`)
475	      for (const error of failures) this.ctx.logger.warn(error)
476	    }
477	  }

479	  /** Remove one provider-owned private temp directory (injectable for cleanup tests). */

481	    const remove = this.internals.rmTempDir ?? ((path: string) => { rmSync(path, { recursive: true, force: true }) })

485	  /**
486	   * Resolve which runner confines commands, once, for the provider's
487	   * lifetime: this platform's chain ({@link PLATFORM_CHAINS}), its sole
488	   * candidate selected directly, multiple candidates arbitrated by
489	   * functional probes in chain order. Fail closed when the platform has no
490	   * chain or no candidate passes — the command never runs.
491	   */
492	  private selectRunner(mode: ConfinedSandboxMode): SelectedRunner {
493	    this.selectedRunner ??= this.chainVerdict()
494	    if (this.selectedRunner === 'unavailable') throw new SandboxUnavailableError(mode)
495	    return this.selectedRunner
496	  }

498	  /** Walk this platform's chain: sole candidate unprobed, several probed in order, none usable → unavailable. */
499	  private chainVerdict(): SelectedRunner | 'unavailable' {
500	    const chain = this.internals.chain ?? PLATFORM_CHAINS[this.internals.platform ?? process.platform] ?? []
501	    const [first, ...rest] = chain
502	    if (first === undefined) return 'unavailable'
503	    // A sole candidate needs no arbitration; its execution-time refusal still fails closed.
504	    if (rest.length === 0) return { runner: first, enforcement: STATIC_ENFORCEMENT[first] }
505	    for (const runner of chain) {
506	      const enforcement = this.probeRunner(runner)
507	      if (enforcement !== 'unusable') return { runner, enforcement }
508	    }
509	    return 'unavailable'
510	  }

512	  /** One rung's functional probe (each at most once, via the chain walk). */
513	  private probeRunner(runner: SelectedRunner['runner']): SandboxEnforcement | 'unusable' {
514	    // bwrap's mount profile and Seatbelt's deny-file-write* profile govern
515	    // every promised file effect by construction, so their passing probes
516	    // are always full enforcement; the Landlock launcher's probe report
517	    // distinguishes full from per-ABI-partial, while windows-acl is always
518	    // partial for its documented Everyone and hard-link boundaries.
519	    switch (runner) {
520	      case 'bwrap': {
521	        const probe = this.internals.probeBwrap ?? (() => defaultProbeBwrap(this.probeTimeoutMs))
522	        return probe() ? 'full' : 'unusable'
523	      }
524	      case 'landlock': {
525	        const probe = this.internals.probeLandlock ?? (launcher => defaultProbeLandlock(launcher, { timeoutMs: this.probeTimeoutMs }))
526	        return probe(this.landlockLauncher())
527	      }
528	      case 'seatbelt': {
529	        const probe = this.internals.probeSeatbelt ?? (exec => defaultProbeSeatbelt(exec, this.probeTimeoutMs))
530	        return probe(this.seatbeltExec()) ? 'full' : 'unusable'
531	      }
532	      case 'windows-acl': {
533	        const probe = this.internals.probeWindowsAcl
534	          ?? (() => defaultProbeWindowsAcl(this.windowsAclRunnerInvocation(), this.probeTimeoutMs))
535	        return probe() ? 'partial' : 'unusable'
536	      }
537	      default: return assertNever(runner)
538	    }
539	  }

547	  private seatbeltExec(): string {

553	   * present (production), else the package source through tsx (development).
554	   * The prefix stays `[node, runner, ...]` — a future native-exe runner keeps

47	 * (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-sandbox`) can never drift apart.

49	 * @returns sandbox-exec arguments before the trailing separator and command argv.
50	 */
51	export function seatbeltProfileArgs(policy: SandboxPolicy): string[] {
52	  const forms = ['(version 1)', '(allow default)', '(deny file-write*)', `(allow file-write* (literal ${sbplString('/dev/null')}))`]
53	  const roots = writableRoots(policy)
54	  if (roots.length > 0) {
55	    forms.push(`(allow file-write* ${roots.map(root => `(subpath ${sbplString(root)})`).join(' ')})`)
56	  }
57	  return ['-p', forms.join(' ')]

1	/**
2	 * The certificate precondition over recorded enforcement: what one session's
3	 * durable record proves about the isolation a certificate may claim.
4	 *
5	 * Decided over the session log alone, so the live refusal in `recordRun` and
6	 * the replay refusal in the `./invariant` companion are the same rule applied
7	 * to the same evidence. A live barrier would add nothing: everything it knows
8	 * about a session is already in the `read-barrier/scope` census it appended
9	 * before that session's first request.
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-verification/isolation
11	 */
12	
13	import { assertNever } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
14	// Type-only: resolves the read-barrier members of the session event vocabulary.
15	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
16	import type { ReadBarrierScope } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier/types'
17	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
18	import type { CertificateIsolation, RunExecutor } from './types.ts'
19	
20	/**
21	 * The census the barrier recorded for one session, absent when no barrier is
22	 * composed. Read newest-first; the barrier's own companion rejects a session
23	 * that records a second one.
24	 * @param events - the session log, oldest first.
25	 * @returns the recorded census, or undefined when the session has none.
26	 */
27	export function recordedScope(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): ReadBarrierScope | undefined {
28	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
29	    const event = events[index]
30	    if (event?.type === 'read-barrier/scope') return event.data
31	  }
32	  return undefined
33	}
34	
35	/**
36	 * Why the recorded census cannot back any certificate, or undefined when it
37	 * can. Applied at every level: composing a tool that carries an authority
38	 * forfeits the certificate even at `none`, and a tool assembled into a request
39	 * the census does not cover means the census stopped describing the session.
40	 * @param events - the session log, oldest first.
41	 * @param scope - the census recorded for that session.
42	 * @returns the reason, or undefined when the census holds.
43	 */
44	function censusProblem(events: readonly SessionEvent[], scope: ReadBarrierScope): string | undefined {
45	  for (const entry of scope.census) {
46	    const [authority] = entry.authority
47	    if (authority !== undefined) {
48	      return `the session composed "${entry.name}", which carries the "${authority}" authority`
49	    }
50	  }
51	  const covered = new Set(scope.census.map(entry => entry.name))
52	  for (const event of events) {
53	    if (event.type !== 'request/header') continue
54	    for (const tool of event.data.header.tools ?? []) {
55	      if (!covered.has(tool.name)) {
56	        return `request/header at event ${String(event.seq)} assembled "${tool.name}", which the scope census does not cover`
57	      }
58	    }
59	  }
60	  return undefined
61	}
62	
63	/**
64	 * Why the record does not prove that no executor of this session opened a
65	 * denied path, or undefined when it does.
66	 * @param scope - the census recorded for the session, absent when none is.
67	 * @returns the reason, or undefined when process-level isolation is proved.
68	 */
69	function executorProblem(scope: ReadBarrierScope | undefined): string | undefined {
70	  if (scope === undefined) return 'no read-barrier/scope records what this session composed'
71	  if (scope.role !== 'implementer') {
72	    return `the session held role "${scope.role}", so no executor denied it a read`
73	  }
74	  for (const entry of scope.enforcement) {
75	    if (entry.state === 'unenforced') {
76	      return `capability "${entry.capability}" is composed without read-barrier enforcement`
77	    }
78	  }
79	  return undefined
80	}
81	
82	/**
83	 * Why the record does not prove the checks are outside this account's write
84	 * reach, or undefined when it does.
85	 * @param events - the session log, oldest first.
86	 * @returns the reason, or undefined when a verified attestation is recorded.
87	 */
88	function attestationProblem(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): string | undefined {
89	  if (events.some(event => event.type === 'read-barrier/attestation')) return undefined
90	  return 'no verified read-barrier/attestation places the standard outside this account'
91	}
92	
93	/**
94	 * Why the run's executor cannot support a claim above `none`, or undefined when
95	 * it can. An `agent-reported` run is the implementer's own account of its
96	 * checks: it is admissible evidence only at the level that asserts nothing.
97	 * @param executor - the executor of the run the certificate cites.
98	 * @returns the reason, or undefined when a validator executed the checks.
99	 */
100	function reportedProblem(executor: RunExecutor): string | undefined {
101	  if (executor === 'runner') return undefined
102	  return 'the run was agent-reported, so no validator executed its checks'
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Why the session's durable record does not support `isolation`, or undefined
107	 * when it does. A session with no census may still certify at `none`, which is
108	 * exactly what that level asserts: nothing.
109	 * @param events - the session log, oldest first.
110	 * @param isolation - the level the caller wants the certificate to claim.
111	 * @param executor - the executor of the run the certificate would cite.
112	 * @returns the reason to refuse, or undefined when the claim is supported.
113	 */
114	export function isolationProblem(
115	  events: readonly SessionEvent[],
116	  isolation: CertificateIsolation,
117	  executor: RunExecutor,
118	): string | undefined {
119	  const scope = recordedScope(events)
120	  const census = scope === undefined ? undefined : censusProblem(events, scope)
121	  if (census !== undefined) return census
122	  switch (isolation) {
123	    case 'none':
124	      return undefined
125	    case 'process':
126	      return reportedProblem(executor) ?? executorProblem(scope)
127	    case 'host':
128	      return reportedProblem(executor) ?? executorProblem(scope) ?? attestationProblem(events)
129	    default:
130	      return assertNever(isolation)
131	  }
132	}

1	/**
2	 * Pure vocabulary of the read barrier: the session roles, the path-opening
3	 * capabilities that can refuse a read, the resolved per-session policy, the
4	 * durable refusal record, the composition census one session was granted, and
5	 * the host attestation that puts the checks outside the harness account.
6	 *
7	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier/types
8	 */
9	
10	import type { ToolAuthority } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools/types'
11	
12	/**
13	 * Authority a session holds against the barrier. `implementer` is denied every
14	 * directory the barrier owns; `validator` and `unrestricted` are denied
15	 * nothing, and `unrestricted` is what a session holds without a reservation.
16	 * Which directories a role may read is a security invariant, never a
17	 * deployment choice.
18	 */
19	export type ReadBarrierRole = 'implementer' | 'validator' | 'unrestricted'
20	
21	/**
22	 * Capability seam that refused one read. Each member names a seam that opens
23	 * paths and can therefore decide a refusal in the operation that opens them.
24	 */
25	export type ReadBarrierCapability = 'fs' | 'shell' | 'subprocess' | 'terminal'
26	
27	/**
28	 * The barrier's complete decision inputs for one session, resolved once per
29	 * capability call. `denied` lists every directory the role may not read,
30	 * canonicalized only at the moment of the containment test.
31	 */
32	export interface ReadBarrierPolicy {
33	  /** Authority the calling session holds. */
34	  readonly role: ReadBarrierRole
35	  /** The barrier's own validator-owned root, always the first denied directory. */
36	  readonly root: string
37	  /** Every denied directory: the root, the configured extras, and the registered ones. */
38	  readonly denied: readonly string[]

40	
41	/**
42	 * One refusal, as the `read-barrier/denied` session event carries it. The path
43	 * is already in the log inside the model's own `tool/call` arguments, so the
44	 * record adds evidence and no new disclosure.
45	 */
46	export interface ReadBarrierDenial {
47	  /** Self-declared payload version. */
48	  readonly version: 1
49	  /** Role the refused session held. */
50	  readonly role: ReadBarrierRole
51	  /** Seam that refused the read. */
52	  readonly capability: ReadBarrierCapability
53	  /** Model-facing path of the refused target, exactly as the refusal reported it. */

56	  readonly root: string

58	
59	/**
60	 * What a preset roster declares about one agent's composition. The roster is
61	 * the only authority that can raise or lower a session's role, because only
62	 * the composition knows which preset was actually mounted.
63	 */
64	export interface ReadBarrierComposition {
65	  /** Preset the agent joined, recorded verbatim in the scope census. */
66	  readonly presetId: string
67	  /**
68	   * Role the preset declared, absent when it declared none. A preset that
69	   * declares no role leaves the reservation to decide, so a validator can
70	   * still make an unmarked composition the implementer.
71	   */
72	  readonly role?: ReadBarrierRole

74	
75	/**
76	 * Path-opening capability the scope census reports enforcement for. It extends
77	 * {@link ReadBarrierCapability} with the two executors the harness cannot fence
78	 * in-process and must therefore refuse to start instead of denying a read.
79	 */
80	export type ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability = ReadBarrierCapability | 'subagent' | 'workflow'
81	
82	/**
83	 * What one path-opening capability does about the barrier in this composition:
84	 * it denies at the operation that opens paths, it is composed and denies
85	 * nothing, or the composition does not have it at all.
86	 */
87	export type ReadBarrierEnforcementState = 'denied-at-executor' | 'unenforced' | 'not-composed'
88	
89	/** One capability's enforcement decision, as the scope census records it. */
90	export interface ReadBarrierEnforcementEntry {
91	  /** The path-opening capability. */
92	  readonly capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability
93	  /** What that capability does about the barrier. */
94	  readonly state: ReadBarrierEnforcementState
95	}
96	
97	/** One visible tool and the authorities its definition declares. */
98	export interface ReadBarrierCensusEntry {
99	  /** Tool name as the session's registry view resolves it. */
100	  readonly name: string
101	  /** Authorities the definition declared, empty for an ordinary tool. */
102	  readonly authority: readonly ToolAuthority[]
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * The composition one session was granted, as the `read-barrier/scope` event
107	 * carries it. Appended before the session's first `request/header`, so the
108	 * census is the durable answer to what the model could reach, and a tool that
109	 * appears in a later header without appearing here was added after the census.
110	 */
111	export interface ReadBarrierScope {
112	  /** Self-declared payload version. */
113	  readonly version: 1
114	  /** Role the session holds for the whole run. */
115	  readonly role: ReadBarrierRole
116	  /** Preset the session composed, absent when the deployment mounts no roster. */
117	  readonly presetId?: string
118	  /** The barrier root in force. */
119	  readonly root: string
120	  /** Every denied directory at census time. */
121	  readonly denied: readonly string[]
122	  /** One entry per tool visible to the agent, in registry order. */
123	  readonly census: readonly ReadBarrierCensusEntry[]
124	  /** One entry per path-opening capability, in a fixed capability order. */
125	  readonly enforcement: readonly ReadBarrierEnforcementEntry[]
126	}
127	
128	/**
129	 * One verified host attestation, as the `read-barrier/attestation` event
130	 * carries it. The barrier writes it only after a file at the configured path
131	 * proved to be owned by another account and unwritable by this one, which is
132	 * the property an in-process component cannot produce for itself.
133	 */
134	export interface ReadBarrierAttestation {
135	  /** Self-declared payload version. */
136	  readonly version: 1
137	  /** Absolute path of the verified file. */
138	  readonly path: string
139	  /** Numeric owner of the file, always different from this process's effective uid. */
140	  readonly owner: number
141	  /** SHA-256 hex digest of the verified file's bytes. */
142	  readonly sha256: string
143	}

3	 * implementer session must not perform, in the role `dsh-sandbox-policy` plays
4	 * for sandbox mode and workspace root. It owns one validator-owned directory

246	    root: z.string(),
247	    denyRoots: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
248	    hostAttestation: z.string(),
249	  })
250	
251	  /** The absolute directory the barrier owns; always the first denied directory. */
252	  readonly root: string
253	
254	  /** Absolute directories denied alongside {@link root} by deployment config. */
255	  private readonly configuredDenyRoots: readonly string[]
256	
257	  /** Absolute path of the file an external account writes, absent when none is configured. */
258	  private readonly hostAttestation: string | undefined
259	
260	  /** Registered denied directories, keyed per registration so two registrations of one path both hold. */
261	  private readonly protectedRoots = new Map<object, string>()
262	
263	  /** Reserved run directory per session; holding one is what makes a session the implementer. */
264	  private readonly reservations = new Map<SessionId, string>()
265	
266	  /** Composition a preset roster declared per session; a declared role outranks a reservation. */
267	  private readonly compositions = new Map<SessionId, ReadBarrierComposition>()
268	
269	  /** Capabilities that registered enforcement, keyed per registration so two registrations both hold. */
270	  private readonly enforcing = new Map<object, ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability>()
271	
272	  /** Sessions whose scope census is already durable, so the census is appended exactly once. */
273	  private readonly censused = new Set<SessionId>()
274	
275	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
276	    super(ctx, 'readBarrier')
277	    this.root = absoluteDirectory(config.root ?? dshHomePath('verification'), 'root')
278	    // schemastery (static Config) already filled `denyRoots`; the cast records
279	    // that runtime fact. `root` has NO schema default, so its fallback to the
280	    // harness home is real branching, resolved absolute either way.
281	    this.configuredDenyRoots = (config.denyRoots as string[]).map(entry => absoluteDirectory(entry, 'denyRoots entry'))
282	    this.hostAttestation = config.hostAttestation === undefined
283	      ? undefined
284	      : absoluteDirectory(config.hostAttestation, 'hostAttestation')
285	    createOwnerOnlyRoot(this.root)
286	    ctx.on('agent/created', ({ agent }) => { this.installGuard(agent) })
287	    // The census is taken here rather than at creation because a validator
288	    // reserves AFTER the agent exists: the role is settled by the time the
289	    // first request is composed, and this waterfall runs before the loop
290	    // appends that request's `request/header`.
291	    ctx.on('agent/request', async ({ agent }, next) => {
292	      this.recordScope(agent)
293	      return await next()
294	    })
295	    ctx.on('agent/disposed', ({ agent }) => {
296	      // The role belongs to the live session: a disposed agent can no longer
297	      // read, and keeping its reservation would grow the map for a process
298	      // running many environments.
299	      this.reservations.delete(agent.id)
300	      this.compositions.delete(agent.id)
301	      this.censused.delete(agent.id)
302	    })
303	  }
304	
305	  /**
306	   * Mint the run directory for one agent's session and record that session as
307	   * the implementer. The validator writes its standard snapshot, one script per
308	   * check, and any held-out fixture there, so the command line the implementer
309	   * can observe in a process listing names a file whose content it cannot read.
310	   * Reserving the same session twice returns the same directory.
311	   *
312	   * Synchronous so the role is in force the moment the caller returns: an
313	   * awaited reservation would leave a window in which the session's own reads
314	   * are still unrestricted.
315	   * @param agent - the implementer agent whose session the run belongs to.
316	   * @returns the absolute run directory, created owner-only.
317	   */
318	  reserve(agent: Agent): string {
319	    const existing = this.reservations.get(agent.id)
320	    if (existing !== undefined) return existing
321	    const directory = join(this.root, RUNS_DIR, agent.id)
322	    mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
323	    this.reservations.set(agent.id, directory)
324	    return directory
325	  }
326	
327	  /**
328	   * Deny one more directory for as long as the registration lives, so a plugin
329	   * that owns a directory contributes it as an effect instead of a deployment
330	   * repeating it in configuration.
331	   * @param path - absolute or `~`-prefixed directory to deny.
332	   * @returns the registration's disposer.
333	   */
334	  protect(path: string): () => void {
335	    const directory = absoluteDirectory(path, 'protect path')
336	    const registration = {}
337	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
338	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {
339	      this.protectedRoots.set(registration, directory)
340	      return () => { this.protectedRoots.delete(registration) }
341	    }, `read-barrier protected root ${directory}`)
342	  }
343	
344	  /**
345	   * Record that one capability denies the barrier's directories in the
346	   * operation that opens paths, for as long as the registration lives. The
347	   * scope census reports a composed capability without one as `unenforced`, and
348	   * an isolation claim above `none` is refused while any such entry stands.
349	   * @param capability - the path-opening capability that enforces.
350	   * @returns the registration's disposer.
351	   */
352	  enforce(capability: ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability): () => void {
353	    const registration = {}
354	    // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-misused-promises -- synchronous cleanup; direct return preserves disposer identity
355	    return this.ctx.effect(() => {
356	      this.enforcing.set(registration, capability)
357	      return () => { this.enforcing.delete(registration) }
358	    }, `read-barrier enforcement ${capability}`)
359	  }
360	
361	  /**
362	   * Record what a preset roster composed for one agent. A declared role
363	   * outranks a reservation, because only the composition knows what was
364	   * actually mounted; a preset that declares none leaves the reservation to
365	   * decide. The roster is the only caller: nothing a session itself runs may
366	   * raise its own role.
367	   * @param agent - the agent whose composition was resolved.
368	   * @param composition - the preset id and the role it declared, if any.
369	   */
370	  declareComposition(agent: Agent, composition: ReadBarrierComposition): void {
371	    this.compositions.set(agent.id, composition)
372	  }
373	
374	  /**
375	   * Resolve the complete policy for one capability call. A session whose preset
376	   * declared a role holds that role; otherwise a session holding a reservation
377	   * is the implementer, and every other session and every agentless call is
378	   * unrestricted.
379	   * @param request - the calling session, when there is one.
380	   * @returns the role, the barrier root, and every denied directory.
381	   */
382	  resolve(request: ReadBarrierRequest = {}): ReadBarrierPolicy {
383	    return {
384	      role: this.roleOf(request.session),
385	      root: this.root,
386	      denied: [...new Set([this.root, ...this.configuredDenyRoots, ...this.protectedRoots.values()])],
387	    }
388	  }
389	
390	  /** The role one session holds: the preset's declaration first, then the reservation. */
391	  private roleOf(session: Session | undefined): ReadBarrierRole {
392	    if (session === undefined) return 'unrestricted'
393	    const declared = this.compositions.get(session.id)?.role
394	    if (declared !== undefined) return declared
395	    return this.reservations.has(session.id) ? 'implementer' : 'unrestricted'
396	  }
397	
398	  /**
399	   * One entry per path-opening capability: `denied-at-executor` when the
400	   * capability registered enforcement, `unenforced` when it is composed without
401	   * one, and `not-composed` when this composition does not have it.
402	   * @returns the enforcement census in the fixed capability order.
403	   */
404	  enforcementCensus(): ReadBarrierEnforcementEntry[] {
405	    const enforced = new Set(this.enforcing.values())
406	    return Object.entries(ENFORCED_CAPABILITY_SERVICES).map(([capability, service]) => ({
407	      capability: capability as ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability,
408	      state: enforced.has(capability as ReadBarrierEnforcedCapability)
409	        ? 'denied-at-executor'
410	        : this.ctx.get(service) === undefined ? 'not-composed' : 'unenforced',
411	    }))
412	  }
413	
414	  /** One census entry per tool the agent's registry view resolves, with the authorities each declares. */
415	  private toolCensus(agent: Agent): ReadBarrierCensusEntry[] {
416	    const tools = agent.ctx.get('tools')
417	    if (tools === undefined) return []
418	    return tools.schemas(agent).map(schema => ({
419	      name: schema.name,
420	      authority: [...tools.get(schema.name, agent)?.authority ?? []],
421	    }))
422	  }
423	
424	  /**
425	   * Append this session's composition census, and its host attestation when one
426	   * verifies, exactly once. Called before the loop composes the session's first
427	   * `request/header`, so the census is durable before any tool schema reaches a
428	   * model.
429	   */
430	  private recordScope(agent: Agent): void {
431	    if (this.censused.has(agent.id)) return
432	    this.censused.add(agent.id)
433	    const composition = this.compositions.get(agent.id)
434	    const scope: ReadBarrierScope = {
435	      version: READ_BARRIER_SCOPE_VERSION,
436	      role: this.roleOf(agent.session),
437	      ...composition === undefined ? {} : { presetId: composition.presetId },
438	      root: this.root,
439	      denied: this.resolve({ session: agent.session }).denied,
440	      census: this.toolCensus(agent),
441	      enforcement: this.enforcementCensus(),
442	    }
443	    agent.session.append('read-barrier/scope', scope)
444	    const attestation = this.verifiedAttestation()
445	    /* v8 ignore start -- only a file owned by another operating-system account reaches this append,
446	       which an unprivileged test process cannot create; `attestationProblem` covers every decision
447	       the record depends on. */
448	    if (attestation !== undefined) agent.session.append('read-barrier/attestation', attestation)
449	    /* v8 ignore stop */
450	  }
451	
452	  /**
453	   * Verify the configured host attestation file.
454	   * @returns the record to append, or undefined when no file is configured, it
455	   * cannot be read, or it does not prove another account owns it.
456	   */
457	  private verifiedAttestation(): ReadBarrierAttestation | undefined {
458	    const path = this.hostAttestation
459	    if (path === undefined) return undefined
460	    let file: AttestationFile
461	    try {
462	      const stats = statSync(path)
463	      file = {
464	        uid: stats.uid,
465	        mode: stats.mode,
466	        isFile: stats.isFile(),
467	        sha256: createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(path)).digest('hex'),
468	      }
469	    } catch {
470	      // An absent or unreadable attestation file is simply no attestation: the
471	      // claim it would have supported is refused instead of the run failing.
472	      this.ctx.logger.warn(`read-barrier: host attestation ${path} cannot be read; no certificate may claim host isolation`)
473	      return undefined
474	    }
475	    const problem = attestationProblem(file, process.geteuid?.())
476	    /* v8 ignore start -- the verifying arm needs a file owned by another operating-system account,
477	       which an unprivileged test process cannot create; `attestationProblem` covers every decision
478	       this arm depends on. */
479	    if (problem === undefined) {
480	      return { version: READ_BARRIER_ATTESTATION_VERSION, path, owner: file.uid, sha256: file.sha256 }
481	    }
482	    /* v8 ignore stop */
483	    this.ctx.logger.warn(`read-barrier: host attestation ${path} ${problem}; no certificate may claim host isolation`)
484	    return undefined
485	  }
486	
487	  /**
488	   * Register this agent's authority guard on its own scope, so a tool
489	   * registered into the agent's layer after its preset mounted is refused at
490	   * execution even though no composition audit saw it.
491	   */
492	  private installGuard(agent: Agent): void {
493	    // Registered through the AGENT's context: `tools.guard()` scopes the effect
494	    // to the caller's context, so the guard covers exactly this agent and
495	    // unwinds with it.
496	    agent.ctx.get('tools')?.guard(execution => this.guardExecution(agent, execution))
497	  }
498	
499	  /** Deny one execution whose definition carries an authority this session's role forbids. */
500	  private guardExecution(agent: Agent, execution: Readonly<ToolExecution>): string | undefined {
501	    const definition = agent.ctx.get('tools')?.get(execution.name, agent)
502	    const denied = deniedAuthority(this.roleOf(agent.session), definition?.authority)
503	    return denied === undefined ? undefined : authorityDenialMessage(execution.name, denied)
504	  }
505	
506	  /**
507	   * Decide whether the policy denies reading one resolved target. Each denied
508	   * directory is canonicalized through the filesystem seam immediately before
509	   * its containment test, so an ancestor symlink swapped since the target was
510	   * resolved is caught. A target whose containment cannot be decided is denied.
511	   * @param policy - the policy {@link resolve} returned for this call.
512	   * @param target - the already-resolved target the caller is about to read.
513	   * @returns true when the read must be refused.
514	   */
515	  async denies(policy: ReadBarrierPolicy, target: FsTarget): Promise<boolean> {
516	    if (policy.role !== 'implementer') return false
517	    for (const denied of policy.denied) {
518	      let directory: FsTarget
519	      try {
520	        directory = await this.ctx.fs.resolve(denied)
521	      } catch {
522	        // A denied directory the backend cannot resolve leaves containment
523	        // undecidable, and an undecidable read fails closed.
524	        return true
525	      }
526	      if (this.ctx.fs.contains(directory, target)) return true
527	    }
528	    return false
529	  }
530	
531	  /**
532	   * Append the durable record of one refusal. The barrier owns the write so
533	   * every seam that refuses produces the same evidence.
534	   * @param session - the refused session, whose log receives the record.
535	   * @param policy - the policy that refused, supplying the role and root.
536	   * @param capability - the seam that refused the read.
537	   * @param target - the refused target, supplying the model-facing path.
538	   * @returns the payload exactly as it was appended.
539	   */
540	  recordDenial(
541	    session: Session,
542	    policy: ReadBarrierPolicy,
543	    capability: ReadBarrierCapability,
544	    target: FsTarget,
545	  ): ReadBarrierDenial {
546	    const denial: ReadBarrierDenial = {
547	      version: READ_BARRIER_DENIED_VERSION,
548	      role: policy.role,
549	      capability,
550	      displayPath: target.displayPath,
551	      root: policy.root,
552	    }
553	    session.append('read-barrier/denied', denial)
554	    return denial
555	  }
556	}
557	
558	export default ReadBarrierService

# native/

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Native source and public packages maintained with DeepSeek Harness. The [`landlock-run/` workspace](landlock-run/README.md) owns the Landlock self-restrict-then-exec launcher consumed by the harness, including its architecture, three-package npm family, platform support, development workflow, and [release procedure](landlock-run/docs/release.md).

## Workspace and release boundary

`landlock-run/` and its packages belong to the repository's root pnpm workspace and lockfile. Harness consumers use the current workspace entry package during development and CI, so a launcher contract change and its consumer update can land and be tested together.

The main repository's `Landlock Run` workflow builds and tests each supported architecture. `Landlock Run Release` assembles those native artifacts, packs and verifies the three npm tarballs, then optionally publishes them under one launcher version. The entry package retains platform packages as npm optional dependencies, so npm still installs only the package matching the user's operating system and CPU.

1	/**
2	 * The JavaScript API over the prebuilt `landlock-run` launcher: resolve the
3	 * binary for this host, build its grant argv, and run its functional probe.
4	 *
5	 * This module owns the launcher's CLI contract (`docs/cli-contract.md`) so
6	 * consumers never parse launcher output or spell launcher flags themselves —
7	 * the contract and the binaries version together in one package family,
8	 * which makes probe-parsing drift against the binary structurally
9	 * impossible. Policy stays with the consumer: this package does not know
10	 * what a "sandbox mode" is, only which paths are granted read or write.
11	 *
12	 * Deliberately no environment-variable overrides anywhere in this module:
13	 * which binary confines a process must never be decidable by the ambient
14	 * environment. Test injection is by function parameter.
15	 */
16	import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
17	import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
18	import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
19	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
20	
21	/** The launcher binary's file name inside each platform package's `bin/`. */
22	export const LAUNCHER_BIN = 'landlock-run'
23	
24	/**
25	 * The exit code for every launcher-level failure (usage error, unenforcing
26	 * kernel, unopenable grant root, failed exec). After a successful `exec`, the
27	 * wrapped command may also return 125, so consumers also require a matching
28	 * launcher-owned fatal diagnostic to attribute launcher failure. Part of the
29	 * CLI contract.
30	 */
31	export const LAUNCHER_FAILURE_EXIT = 125
32	
33	/**
34	 * The probe's verdict on this host: `full` when the running kernel enforces
35	 * every access the launcher can govern, `partial` when an older Landlock ABI
36	 * governs only a subset (still confined for everything it supports), and
37	 * `unusable` when nothing can be enforced — a kernel without Landlock, a
38	 * disabled LSM, or a missing binary, all indistinguishable on purpose
39	 * because the consumer's answer is the same: do not trust this launcher.
40	 */
41	export type LandlockEnforcement = 'full' | 'partial' | 'unusable'
42	
43	/**
44	 * Filesystem grants for one confined run. Everything not granted is denied —
45	 * Landlock rulesets are allow-lists.
46	 */
47	export interface LauncherGrants {
48	  /** Roots granted read + execute beneath (the launcher's `--ro`). */
49	  readonly readOnly?: readonly string[]
50	  /** Roots granted full filesystem access beneath (the launcher's `--rw`). */
51	  readonly readWrite?: readonly string[]
52	}
53	
54	/**
55	 * Path of the launcher binary for this host: resolved from the per-platform
56	 * npm package `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run-<platform>-<arch>` (npm's
57	 * `os`/`cpu` fields make installers fetch only the matching one). When the
58	 * package is not resolvable — a platform without one, or an install that
59	 * skipped the optional dependency — the returned fallback path points inside
60	 * this package's own `node_modules` and simply never exists. Existence is
61	 * deliberately not checked either way: {@link probe} is the single
62	 * availability signal (a missing binary probes `unusable` the same way an
63	 * unenforcing kernel does).
64	 * @param resolvePackageJson - test hook over `require.resolve` (the default
65	 *   covers real installs); receives the platform package's `package.json`
66	 *   specifier and returns its absolute path, throwing when unresolvable.
67	 * @returns the absolute launcher path to probe and exec.
68	 */
69	export function launcherPath(
70	  resolvePackageJson: (specifier: string) => string = createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve,
71	): string {
72	  const platformPackage = `@deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run-${process.platform}-${process.arch}`
73	  try {
74	    return join(dirname(resolvePackageJson(`${platformPackage}/package.json`)), 'bin', LAUNCHER_BIN)
75	  } catch {
76	    // Unresolvable platform package: no such package exists for this host, or
77	    // it was not installed. Fall back to the path pnpm's layout WOULD use —
78	    // absolute, inside this package's boundary (never cwd-relative: a
79	    // spawnable relative path here would hand cwd control over which binary
80	    // confines), and nonexistent exactly when the package is absent.
81	    return fileURLToPath(new URL(`../node_modules/${platformPackage}/bin/${LAUNCHER_BIN}`, import.meta.url))
82	  }
83	}
84	
85	/**
86	 * The launcher grant arguments for one set of filesystem grants — everything
87	 * before the `--` argv separator. A caller spawns
88	 * `[launcherPath(), ...grantArgs(grants), '--', ...command]`; the flag
89	 * spellings stay private to this package.
90	 * @param grants - the read-only and read-write roots to allow.
91	 * @returns the `--ro <path>` / `--rw <path>` argument list, read-only roots
92	 *   first, in the caller's order.
93	 */
94	export function grantArgs(grants: LauncherGrants): string[] {
95	  return [
96	    ...(grants.readOnly ?? []).flatMap(root => ['--ro', root]),
97	    ...(grants.readWrite ?? []).flatMap(root => ['--rw', root]),
98	  ]
99	}
100	
101	/**
102	 * Functional probe: `landlock-run --probe` builds and enforces a maximal
103	 * ruleset in a short-lived child and exits 0 only when the running kernel
104	 * actually enforces it — `--version`-style checks would miss a kernel that
105	 * has the syscalls but refuses enforcement. The probe's one report line is
106	 * part of the CLI contract and distinguishes complete from per-ABI-subset
107	 * enforcement; a zero exit without the partial marker reads as `full`. A
108	 * failed or timed-out spawn (missing binary, wrong architecture, unenforcing
109	 * kernel) probes `unusable`. Synchronous by design: consumers run it once
110	 * and cache the verdict.
111	 * @param launcher - the launcher path to probe; defaults to
112	 *   {@link launcherPath}'s resolution for this host.
113	 * @param options - `timeoutMs` bounds the probe child (default 2000).
114	 * @returns the enforcement verdict for this host.
115	 */
116	export function probe(
117	  launcher: string = launcherPath(),
118	  options: { timeoutMs?: number } = {},
119	): LandlockEnforcement {
120	  const result = spawnSync(launcher, ['--probe'], {
121	    timeout: options.timeoutMs ?? 2000,
122	    encoding: 'utf8',
123	    stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'ignore'],
124	  })
125	  if (result.status !== 0) return 'unusable'
126	  return /partially enforced/.test(result.stdout) ? 'partial' : 'full'
127	}

1	/**
2	 * Sandbox-consuming bash executor. It wraps the exact local bash argv through
3	 * `ctx.sandbox`, inherits local process mechanics, and reports the selected
4	 * mode, enforcement, and denial facts. Positive runner-launch evidence means
5	 * the command never ran: foreground calls throw `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE`, while
6	 * background processes carry `runnerFailed`; other spawn rejections retain
7	 * local-executor semantics. The tool owns approval and passes a complete per-call policy.
8	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-sandbox
9	 */
10	
11	import { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
12	import type { ShellExecRequest, ShellExecSpec, ShellProcess, ShellRunResult } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-shell'
13	import { SandboxUnavailableError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox'
14	import type {
15	  ConfinedArgv,
16	  ConfinedSandboxMode,
17	  RunnerFailureRule,
18	  SandboxEnforcement,
19	  SandboxExecutionPolicy,
20	  SandboxMode,
21	  SandboxPolicy,
22	} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox'
23	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy'
24	import { LocalBashExecutor } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'
25	import type { Config as LocalConfig } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-local'
26	import { classifyDenial, classifyRunnerFailure, isRunnerSpawnFailure, matchesSignature } from './helpers.ts'
27	
28	/**
29	 * Plugin config: the local executor's knobs, verbatim. The sandbox policy —
30	 * the default mode and fallback `workspace-write` root — is NOT here: it lives
31	 * on `ctx.sandboxPolicy` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy`), which resolves
32	 * each calling session's mode and cwd for every enforcing capability. The runner
33	 * choice is likewise the `ctx.sandbox` provider's config, not this executor's.
34	 */
35	export type Config = LocalConfig
36	
37	/**
38	 * Registers as `ctx.shell` in place of the local executor and requires a
39	 * `ctx.sandbox` provider plus `ctx.sandboxPolicy`; the tool layer is
40	 * unchanged. Tool calls pass the calling session's resolved policy; direct
41	 * calls fall back to deployment policy. `result.sandbox` reports the mode and
42	 * enforcement actually used.
43	 */
44	export class SandboxBashExecutor extends LocalBashExecutor {
45	  static override inject = ['subprocess', 'sandbox', 'sandboxPolicy']
46	
47	  // No own Config: the sandbox default (mode + workspaceRoot) is owned by
48	  // ctx.sandboxPolicy, so this executor inherits LocalBashExecutor's Config
49	  // verbatim (the config catalog walks the inherited static).
50	
51	  private readonly mode: SandboxMode
52	  /**
53	   * Per-process confinement facts retained until settlement. Providers may
54	   * vary enforcement and diagnostic dialect between overlapping calls, so a
55	   * shared latest-wrap value would classify a process against the wrong facts.
56	   * Unconfined processes have no entry.
57	   */
58	  private readonly processFacts = new Map<ShellProcess, {
59	    mode: ConfinedSandboxMode
60	    enforcement: SandboxEnforcement
61	    denialSignatures: readonly string[]
62	    runnerFailureRules: readonly RunnerFailureRule[]
63	    runnerProgram: string | undefined
64	    workdir: string
65	  }>()
66	
67	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
68	    super(ctx, config)
69	    // The default mode is the capability fact used for schema advertisement;
70	    // actual tool executions carry their resolved per-call policy.
71	    this.mode = ctx.sandboxPolicy.defaultMode
72	  }
73	
74	  /** The configured default mode — the capability fact the tool layer reads. */
75	  override get sandboxMode(): SandboxMode {
76	    return this.mode
77	  }
78	
79	  /**
80	   * Stamp a complete per-call policy onto the spec. Tool calls supply the
81	   * calling session's resolved mode and root; lower-level callers fall back to
82	   * the deployment policy.
83	   */
84	  override resolve(request: ShellExecRequest): ShellExecSpec {
85	    return { ...super.resolve(request), sandboxPolicy: request.sandboxPolicy ?? this.ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve() }
86	  }
87	
88	  override async run(spec: ShellExecSpec): Promise<ShellRunResult> {
89	    const policy = spec.sandboxPolicy as SandboxExecutionPolicy
90	    const { mode } = policy
91	    if (mode === 'danger-full-access') {
92	      const result = await super.run(spec)
93	      return { ...result, sandbox: { mode, denied: false } }
94	    }
95	    const confined = this.confine(spec.command, { ...policy, mode })
96	    let result: ShellRunResult
97	    try {
98	      result = await this.runArgv(spec, confined.argv)
99	    } catch (error) {
100	      // An upstream abort remains cancellation even when it prevents spawn.
101	      if (spec.signal?.aborted === true) spec.signal.throwIfAborted()
102	      if (isRunnerSpawnFailure(error, confined.argv[0], spec.workdir)) {
103	        throw new SandboxUnavailableError(mode, String(error))
104	      }
105	      throw error
106	    }
107	    // Runner failure outranks denial because the command did not run. Carry
108	    // the matched fatal line, not an informational line that preceded it.
109	    const runnerFailure = classifyRunnerFailure(result.exitCode, result.stderr.text, confined.runnerFailureRules)
110	    if (runnerFailure !== undefined) {
111	      throw new SandboxUnavailableError(mode, runnerFailure.detail)
112	    }
113	    return { ...result, sandbox: { mode, denied: classifyDenial(result, confined.denialSignatures), enforcement: confined.enforcement } }
114	  }
115	
116	  override start(spec: ShellExecSpec): ShellProcess {
117	    const policy = spec.sandboxPolicy as SandboxExecutionPolicy
118	    const { mode } = policy
119	    if (mode === 'danger-full-access') return super.start(spec)
120	    // Once startArgv returns, install facts synchronously; promise settlement
121	    // cannot run before start() returns.
122	    const confined = this.confine(spec.command, { ...policy, mode })
123	    let proc: ShellProcess
124	    try {
125	      proc = this.startArgv(spec, confined.argv)
126	    } catch (error) {
127	      // LocalSubprocessRuntime reports ENOENT/EACCES with the failed executable path through async
128	      // `done` rejection; this covers alternatives that throw the same error synchronously.
129	      if (isRunnerSpawnFailure(error, confined.argv[0], spec.workdir)) {
130	        throw new SandboxUnavailableError(mode, String(error))
131	      }
132	      throw error
133	    }
134	    const { enforcement, denialSignatures, runnerFailureRules } = confined
135	    this.processFacts.set(proc, {
136	      mode,
137	      enforcement,
138	      denialSignatures,
139	      runnerFailureRules,
140	      runnerProgram: confined.argv[0],
141	      workdir: spec.workdir,
142	    })
143	    return proc
144	  }
145	
146	  /**
147	   * Stamp per-process sandbox facts before `done` settles. Full-access processes
148	   * have no facts; signal deaths are not denials.
149	   */
150	  protected override onProcessDone(proc: ShellProcess, stderr: string, spawnFailed: boolean, spawnError?: unknown): void {
151	    const facts = this.processFacts.get(proc)
152	    if (facts !== undefined) {
153	      this.processFacts.delete(proc)
154	      // A rejected spawn never started the confined launch. Otherwise runner
155	      // failure outranks denial because its diagnostics may contain denial terms.
156	      const runnerFailed = spawnFailed
157	        ? isRunnerSpawnFailure(spawnError, facts.runnerProgram, facts.workdir)
158	        : classifyRunnerFailure(proc.exitCode, stderr, facts.runnerFailureRules) !== undefined
159	      proc.sandbox = {
160	        mode: facts.mode,
161	        denied: !runnerFailed && matchesSignature(proc.exitCode, stderr, facts.denialSignatures),
162	        enforcement: facts.enforcement,
163	        ...(runnerFailed ? { runnerFailed } : {}),
164	      }
165	    }
166	    super.onProcessDone(proc, stderr, spawnFailed, spawnError)
167	  }
168	
169	  /**
170	   * Wrap one shell command via the `ctx.sandbox` provider. Provider errors
171	   * propagate unchanged; the returned argv is handed directly to the local
172	   * executor's subprocess path.
173	   * @param command - shell source for the confined inner `bash -c`.
174	   * @param policy - resolved confined execution policy.
175	   * @returns the provider's exact argv and settlement-classification facts.
176	   */
177	  private confine(command: string, policy: SandboxPolicy): ConfinedArgv {
178	    return this.ctx.sandbox.confine(['bash', '-c', command], policy)
179	  }
180	}
181	
182	export default SandboxBashExecutor

1	/**
2	 * Event-only filesystem read policy; it registers no service and declares no
3	 * config, because every deployment-varying value belongs to `ctx.readBarrier`.
4	 * It is the read counterpart of the write and edit policy
5	 * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy` contributes through the same `fs/*`
6	 * event gate: it decides `fs/read-intent`, refusing a target the barrier denies
7	 * to the calling session's role and delegating every other read. See the
8	 * package README for composition rules.
9	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-read-barrier
10	 */
11	
12	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
13	import type { FsReadDenial, FsTarget } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs'
14	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-read-barrier'
15	import type { Session } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import type { FsReadBarrierActor } from './types.ts'
17	
18	export type * from './types.ts'
19	
20	/**
21	 * The complete model-facing account of one refused read. No recovery
22	 * instruction follows it: no retry of the same call succeeds.
23	 * @param displayPath - the model-facing path of the refused target.
24	 * @returns the exact denial message.
25	 */
26	export function readBarrierDenialMessage(displayPath: string): string {
27	  return `read denied: "${displayPath}" is validator-owned — it is not part of this task; continue without it`
28	}
29	
30	/**
31	 * Find the session a read runs for by narrowing the opaque event actor.
32	 * @param actor - the tool-execution context the read executor dispatched with.
33	 * @returns the calling session, or `undefined` for a call with no agent.
34	 */
35	function sessionOf(actor: object | undefined): Session | undefined {
36	  // tsgolint treats object as assignable to weak FsReadBarrierActor, while tsc still requires the structural cast for property access.
37	  // See the analyzer-divergence consequence in .agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-29-oxlint-linter.md.
38	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-unnecessary-type-assertion -- The analyzers disagree on this weak type.
39	  return (actor as FsReadBarrierActor | undefined)?.agent?.session
40	}
41	
42	/** Cordis plugin name used by loader diagnostics. */
43	export const name = 'fs-read-barrier'
44	
45	/** The barrier owns every deployment-varying value this plugin decides from. */
46	export const inject = ['readBarrier']
47	
48	/**
49	 * Decide one dispatched read.
50	 * @param ctx - the plugin context carrying the barrier service.
51	 * @param target - the resolved target the executor is about to read.
52	 * @param actor - the opaque tool-execution context.
53	 * @returns the refusal, or `undefined` to delegate to the next read policy.
54	 */
55	async function decide(ctx: Context, target: FsTarget, actor: object | undefined): Promise<FsReadDenial | undefined> {
56	  const session = sessionOf(actor)
57	  if (session === undefined) return undefined
58	  const policy = ctx.readBarrier.resolve({ session })
59	  if (!await ctx.readBarrier.denies(policy, target)) return undefined
60	  const denial = ctx.readBarrier.recordDenial(session, policy, 'fs', target)
61	  return { code: 'FS_READ_BARRIER_DENIED', message: readBarrierDenialMessage(denial.displayPath) }
62	}
63	
64	/**
65	 * Register the `fs/read-intent` listener.
66	 * @param ctx - the plugin context; the registration is an effect scoped to it.
67	 */
68	export function apply(ctx: Context): void {
69	  // Delegating, not single-slot: a barrier that owned the slot would stop every
70	  // later read policy from deciding. The waterfall is unbound (the executor
71	  // dispatches it with no `this`), so the listener takes the raw arguments.
72	  ctx.on('fs/read-intent', async (target, actor, next) => await decide(ctx, target, actor) ?? await next())
73	  // What makes the scope census report `fs` as `denied-at-executor`: the
74	  // registration lives exactly as long as the listener above.
75	  ctx.readBarrier.enforce('fs')
76	}

# AGENTS.md — Examples

Runnable harness compositions. `examples/` is one workspace member and the module-resolution root for runnable and test Cordis configs; it is not a build target. [package.json](package.json) declares the packages loaded by those configs, while each leaf's private `package.json` remains metadata only.

Extract reusable logic into `packages/`, where per-file coverage and README gates apply. Examples keep only `cordis.yml` wiring, demo artifacts, and e2e/snapshot scenarios; app package bins own boot glue.

## E2E smokes

Each example has both:

- **Keyless:** boot the real `cordis.yml` through the Loader, drive it, and assert output and clean exit. Catches invalid Loader exports that hand-mounted tests miss ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **With-key:** send a live-model prompt and verify external state, not the model's claim. Self-skip without `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`; see [testing.md](../docs/testing.md).

Keyless process smokes use `@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke` for Loader launch resolution; terminal tests wrap that launch in a pseudo-terminal. Tests supply paths, environment, input, and assertions. Every checked-in test Cordis config lives under its corresponding `examples/<agent>/` leaf. Map a package-owned config to `examples/<agent>/tests/fixtures/<group>/<package>/cordis.yml`, keep its driver and assertions package-local, and declare every package it names in both root `tsconfig.json` references and `examples/package.json`.

Do not inventory example tests here; the `tests/` trees and root scripts are authoritative.

In `cordis.yml`, comment only non-obvious wiring, load-order consequences, replay, security boundaries, and configuration scope. Do not narrate visible entries; use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment.

See [the root AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) for repo-wide conventions and [docs/architecture.md](../docs/architecture.md) for the design.

1	/**
2	 * Shared execution plumbing for the `glob` / `grep` search tools: the
3	 * package-owned `SEARCH_*` error vocabulary, one spawn helper that runs the
4	 * PACKAGED ripgrep binary (`@vscode/ripgrep`) with a plain argv vector and
5	 * returns complete raw stdout, the best-effort formatted-result spill handoff,
6	 * and workdir-relative path display.
7	 *
8	 * Both tools execute as ordinary foreground spawns through `ctx.subprocess` —
9	 * never `ctx.shell`, never `ctx.shell.start()`, never a model-visible background
10	 * task. The ripgrep binary ships inside the npm package, so no system `rg`
11	 * install is required, and no shell layer exists between the argv vector and
12	 * ripgrep, so no shell quoting is involved. Raw `rg` stdout is an internal
13	 * transport detail: the tools request a per-run stdout capture budget from the
14	 * subprocess seam, parse only complete in-memory stdout within
15	 * `rawOutputMaxBytes`, and never read spill files. The model-facing recovery
16	 * artifact is the formatted result saved through `ctx.spillStore.saveText()`
17	 * ({@link trySaveFormattedResult}).
18	 *
19	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search/search-core
20	 */
21	
22	import { isAbsolute, relative, sep } from 'node:path'
23	import type { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
24	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
25	import { ItemRetainer, TextRetainer } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-output-retention'
26	import type { RetainedItems } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-output-retention'
27	import type { SubprocessHandle, SubprocessOutcome, SubprocessOutputRead, SubprocessSpawnSpec } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess'
28	import type { SaveTextSpill, SpillRef } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-spill'
29	import type { ToolExecution } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
30	
31	/**
32	 * Default cap on the complete raw `rg` stdout the tools will parse (the
33	 * `rawOutputMaxBytes` config), matching Claude Code's ripgrep raw buffer.
34	 */
35	export const RAW_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES = 20_000_000
36	
37	/**
38	 * Default cooperative tool-call timeout budget in milliseconds (the `timeoutMs`
39	 * config), attached to both tool definitions for
40	 * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy` to enforce through `exec.signal`.
41	 */
42	export const SEARCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000
43	
44	/**
45	 * Default cap in bytes on the retained stderr tail of one search run — a
46	 * diagnostic excerpt only (the tool never reads a stderr spill path, and the
47	 * collect disposition requests none).
48	 */
49	export const SEARCH_STDERR_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024
50	
51	/** Default terminate grace period for a search process (ms). */
52	export const SEARCH_GRACE_MS = 3_000
53	
54	/**
55	 * Default cap in bytes on one search's serialized `presentationMeta` (the
56	 * `searchMetaMaxBytes` config). The inline match/path caps already bound the item
57	 * COUNT, but retained matches of a broad search (many long lines) can still
58	 * serialize to hundreds of kilobytes, and `meta` is persisted with the session
59	 * log and re-sent on every request. A deployment's final output budget
60	 * (`dsh-spill-policy`) only shrinks a result's `content`, never its `meta`, so the
61	 * projection owns this cap. 64 KiB holds the full default-capped result of a
62	 * typical search while bounding the pathological one.
63	 */
64	export const SEARCH_META_MAX_BYTES = 65_536
65	
66	/**
67	 * Stable, machine-routable codes for search failures. Package-owned (not
68	 * `FsErrorCode`) because these tools are spawn-backed discovery, not `ctx.fs`
69	 * provider operations: `SEARCH_INVALID_PATTERN` — ripgrep rejected the regex or
70	 * glob; `SEARCH_FAILED` — the search could not run or its output could not be
71	 * parsed (a failed `rg` launch, inaccessible target, signal kill, malformed
72	 * `--json`); `SEARCH_RAW_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW` — raw `rg` output exceeded
73	 * `rawOutputMaxBytes` or stayed truncated after that requested stdout budget;
74	 * `SEARCH_ABORTED` — the cooperative tool timeout or caller cancellation cut
75	 * the search short.
76	 */
77	export type SearchErrorCode =
78	  | 'SEARCH_INVALID_PATTERN'
79	  | 'SEARCH_FAILED'
80	  | 'SEARCH_RAW_OUTPUT_OVERFLOW'
81	  | 'SEARCH_ABORTED'
82	
83	/**
84	 * Typed search failure. Extends {@link HarnessError} so it carries a stable
85	 * {@link SearchErrorCode} and chains `cause`; the tool registry exposes
86	 * `{ name, code }` on `isError` results so retry/permission/UI layers can
87	 * branch without parsing messages.
88	 */
89	export class SearchError extends HarnessError {
90	  override readonly code: SearchErrorCode
91	
92	  constructor(message: string, code: SearchErrorCode, options?: ErrorOptions) {
93	    super(message, code, options)
94	    this.code = code
95	  }
96	}
